_about: Drafted descriptions for every Customizer setting (October 27 2026), for Ken's review before any go into keyguard.scad. 'tip' appears when pointing at a setting; 'when', 'values' and 'picture' are for the Design Settings Reference; 'question' is for Ken; 'drafter_notes' is what the drafters found in the code, kept for whoever builds the reference. Read back Ken's edits from the review .docx before regenerating it.

settings.name: type_of_keyguard
settings.tip: Whether the keyguard will be 3D-printed or laser-cut from a flat acrylic sheet. Laser-Cut is shown as a 1/8 inch (3.175 millimeter) plate with straight-sided openings and is exported as SVG.
settings.when: Set it to Laser-Cut when the keyguard will be cut from acrylic, for example when it must be clear, extra strong, or too big to print in one piece.
settings.values: Laser-Cut ignores the slope and chamfer settings, so every edge is straight, and leaves off raised features such as ridges. Its only mounting choices are none and Slide-in Tabs, and it can't be split, framed or given cell inserts. Some of these limits relax when use Laser Cutting best practices is no.
settings.picture: 3D-Printed vs Laser-Cut, with cell edge slope = 60 so the sloped and the straight opening walls can be told apart
settings.drafter_notes: By my reading, a Laser-Cut design with a mounting method other than none or Slide-in Tabs (Velcro, say) shows a keyguard in the 3D view but exports no SVG: the 3D view treats the mounting method as none, but the SVG branch checks the method as chosen and falls through to listing the settings (lines 607-609 vs 1846). Not tested.

settings.name: keyguard_thickness
settings.tip: How thick the keyguard is, in millimeters. The area over the screen, where the openings are, follows screen area thickness instead when that is smaller.
settings.when: Change it when the keyguard needs to be stiffer or thinner, or to suit how far the screen sits below the front of the case; raise screen area thickness with it if you want deeper openings.
settings.values: A Laser-Cut keyguard ignores it and is always 3.175 millimeters. With a keyguard frame, it can't be more than keyguard frame thickness. If screen area thickness is larger than this, the screen area is made this thick too.
settings.note: not for use with Laser-Cut keyguards
settings.picture: 3 vs 6, with screen area thickness set to the same value each time; view from the side

settings.name: screen_area_thickness
settings.tip: How thick the keyguard is over the screen, where the grid and bar openings are, in millimeters. Making it thinner than the border gives shallower openings.
settings.when: Lower it when the openings are too deep for the student to reach the screen easily but you want the border of the keyguard to stay at full thickness.
settings.values: The top of the screen area is lowered while its underside stays flat on the screen, so the border stands higher than the area inside it. A number larger than keyguard thickness is treated as keyguard thickness, and a Laser-Cut keyguard ignores it.
settings.note: cannot exceed the keyguard thickness
settings.picture: 4 vs 2, with keyguard thickness = 4

settings.name: generate
settings.tip: What the designer makes and exports: the keyguard, one half of a split keyguard, a clip for Clip-on Straps, a keyguard frame or half of one, a cell insert, or a list of your settings.
settings.when: Change it once the keyguard is designed, to make the other pieces it needs, such as its clips or the second half of a split keyguard.
settings.values: The halves are for a keyguard split to fit a small printer (see Split Keyguard Info); export each in turn. Horizontal clips grip the left and right edges and vertical clips the top and bottom, with mini and micro clips as smaller versions for other strap setups; the frame choices need have a keyguard frame set to yes. Customizer settings makes nothing to print and lists the settings you've changed in the Console.
settings.picture: keyguard vs first half of keyguard
settings.drafter_notes: The web app leaves 'first layer for SVG/DXF file' out of this list (the SVG button makes that layer itself), so the reference should probably not list it as a choice. For a Laser-Cut keyguard the halves, frames and cell insert make nothing but a Console message. The mini and micro clip descriptions come from the Clip-on Straps page (438), not from the code.

settings.name: type_of_tablet
settings.tip: The tablet or AAC device the keyguard is for. It sets the size and position of the screen and where the home button, camera and light sensors are.
settings.when: Set it first for every new design, to the exact model the student uses; the volksswitch.org page What iPad do I have? helps tell iPads apart.
settings.values: Choose blank for a plain plate with no screen, such as a keyguard for a computer keyboard, shaped by the case opening and your case openings. Choose other tablet for a model that isn't listed, and describe it in other tablet general sizes and other tablet pixel sizes in Special Actions and Settings. Systems sold with their own case, such as Accent devices, need have a case set to yes.
settings.picture: iPad 9th generation vs iPad mini 6, with have a case = no
settings.drafter_notes: With blank, screen openings are skipped, so its openings have to be entered as case openings (lines 2321-2325, page 3868).

settings.name: orientation
settings.tip: Whether the student uses the tablet in landscape (wide) or portrait (tall). Measure the case opening, the bars and the screenshot the same way round.
settings.when: Set it to match how the tablet sits in front of the student.
settings.picture: landscape vs portrait

settings.name: expose_home_button
settings.tip: Yes cuts an opening over the tablet's home button so it can be pressed. No covers the button.
settings.when: Set it to no when the student shouldn't be able to press the home button through the keyguard, for example so they stay in the AAC app.
settings.values: Has no effect on tablets without a home button, such as recent iPads.
settings.picture: yes vs no, on iPad 9th generation (a tablet with a home button)

settings.name: home_button_edge_slope
settings.tip: The angle of the home button opening's sloped sides, in degrees. 90 is straight down; a smaller number gives a gentler slope that's easier for a finger to reach into.
settings.when: Lower it if the home button is hard to reach through the keyguard, or raise it toward 90 to make the button harder to press by accident.
settings.values: Only the two sides that run toward the screen slope; the other two stay straight. Laser-Cut keyguards always use 90, and the setting does nothing on tablets without a home button.
settings.picture: 90 vs 30, on iPad 9th generation with expose home button = yes; look at it from the side
settings.drafter_notes: I couldn't confirm the exact shape a round home button's opening takes when only two of its sides slope. The setting has no range or step, so any number can be typed.
settings.source: keyguard.scad 174, 610, 3592-3608, 6402-6438; page 683 for the slope convention

settings.name: expose_camera
settings.tip: Yes cuts an opening over the tablet's front camera, with room around it so the keyguard doesn't block its view. No covers the camera.
settings.when: Leave it at yes unless you'd rather the keyguard covered the camera, for example when nothing the student uses needs it.
settings.values: Has no effect on a tablet the designer has no camera position for.
settings.picture: yes vs no, on iPad 9th generation

settings.name: rotate_tablet_180_degrees
settings.tip: Yes when the tablet is turned the other way round, so its home button, camera and light sensors sit at the opposite ends from where the designer puts them.
settings.when: Set it to yes when the home button or camera on the real tablet is on the opposite side from the one the 3D view shows.
settings.values: In landscape the designer puts an iPad's home button on the right and its camera on the left; yes swaps them. The tablet's borders and corner shapes are turned too, which matters when the screen isn't centered on the tablet.
settings.picture: no vs yes, on iPad 9th generation in landscape (the home button and camera openings swap ends)

settings.name: add_symmetric_openings
settings.tip: Yes repeats the home button, camera and light sensor openings at the opposite end as well, so one keyguard fits whichever way round the tablet is turned.
settings.when: Use it when the tablet doesn't always sit the same way round in its case, so you don't need a separate keyguard for each way.
settings.values: Only openings that are exposed are repeated. It also switches off any case additions that change the keyguard's outline.
settings.note: cannot be used with unequal case opening sides or with keyguard frames
settings.picture: no vs yes, on iPad 9th generation in its case
settings.drafter_notes: By my reading, with have a case set to no it works only when the tablet's built-in borders are exactly equal on both sides; for iPad 9th generation they differ by about 0.01 millimeter, so nothing would be repeated, with no message (lines 1078-1089, 2285). Worth a test. On a Laser-Cut keyguard the repeated light sensor openings are cut even when expose ambient light sensors is no (lines 2486-2492). On a 3D-printed keyguard the repeated light sensor openings are cut to the screen area thickness rather than the full thickness (line 2291); I didn't confirm whether that shows. The case additions it switches off are the full-height ones that reshape the outline (lines 7448-7477).

settings.name: expose_ambient_light_sensors
settings.tip: Yes cuts small openings over the tablet's ambient light sensors, which it uses to adjust screen brightness. No covers them.
settings.when: Leave it at yes unless you have a reason to cover the sensors, since the tablet relies on them to set its brightness automatically.
settings.values: Only tablets the designer has sensor positions for get openings: most iPads, the Via Mini and the Via Pro.
settings.picture: yes vs no, on iPad 9th generation (small round openings beside the camera)
settings.drafter_notes: The Tobii-Dynavox I-16 has sensor positions in the code, but they are looked up under the name 'TobiiDynavox I-16', which doesn't match the menu's 'Tobii-Dynavox I-16', so no openings are cut for it (line 1723 vs line 832). Looks like a bug.

settings.name: have_a_case
settings.tip: Yes if the tablet is in a case: the keyguard is shaped to fit the case opening. No makes a keyguard the size and shape of the whole front of the tablet.
settings.when: Set it to no when the tablet is used without a case.
settings.values: With no, the case opening measurements are ignored and the keyguard follows the tablet's own outline and corners. Systems sold with their own case, such as Accent devices, need yes and the case opening measurements.
settings.picture: yes vs no, on iPad 9th generation

settings.name: height_of_opening_in_case
settings.tip: How tall the opening in the front of the case is, in millimeters, from its top edge to its bottom edge as the student sees the tablet. The keyguard is made this tall.
settings.when: Enter it for every keyguard that goes in a case; measure carefully, since a keyguard that's too big won't lie flat and one that's too small slides around.
settings.values: The openings stay over the screen whatever you enter, because the designer assumes the screen is centered in the case opening. If it isn't, see unequal bottom side of case opening in Special Actions and Settings.
settings.picture: 160 vs 185, with have a case = yes

settings.name: width_of_opening_in_case
settings.tip: How wide the opening in the front of the case is, in millimeters, from its left edge to its right edge as the student sees the tablet. The keyguard is made this wide.
settings.when: Enter it for every keyguard that goes in a case; measure carefully, since a keyguard that's too big won't lie flat and one that's too small slides around.
settings.values: The openings stay over the screen whatever you enter, because the designer assumes the screen is centered in the case opening. If it isn't, see unequal left side of case opening in Special Actions and Settings.
settings.picture: 215 vs 245, with have a case = yes

settings.name: case_opening_corner_radius
settings.tip: The radius of the case opening's rounded corners, in millimeters. The keyguard's corners are rounded to match.
settings.when: Match it to the case; if you're unsure between two sizes, the larger radius is the safer choice.
settings.values: 0 makes square corners. A Laser-Cut keyguard uses at least 2 millimeters while use Laser Cutting best practices is yes.
settings.picture: 0 vs 15, with have a case = yes

settings.name: case_height
settings.tip: The overall height of the case, outside edge to outside edge, in millimeters. It's used only for the clips of Clip-on Straps and for a sloped edge that reaches the edge of the case.
settings.when: Enter it when you mount with Clip-on Straps, or when add sloped keyguard edge and extend lip to edge of case are both yes.
settings.values: With Clip-on Straps, a larger number makes the vertical clips reach farther across the case to the keyguard. With a sloped edge extended to the edge of the case, the keyguard is made this tall.
settings.picture: 200 vs 240, with generate = vertical clip (the clip's reach gets longer)

settings.name: case_width
settings.tip: The overall width of the case, outside edge to outside edge, in millimeters. It's used only for the clips of Clip-on Straps and for a sloped edge that reaches the edge of the case.
settings.when: Enter it when you mount with Clip-on Straps, or when add sloped keyguard edge and extend lip to edge of case are both yes.
settings.values: With Clip-on Straps, a larger number makes the horizontal clips reach farther across the case to the keyguard. With a sloped edge extended to the edge of the case, the keyguard is made this wide.
settings.picture: 260 vs 300, with generate = horizontal clip (the clip's reach gets longer)

settings.name: case_thickness
settings.tip: How thick the case is from front to back, in millimeters. It's used only to size the clips for Clip-on Straps, which wrap around the case's edge.
settings.when: Enter it when you mount the keyguard with Clip-on Straps.
settings.values: A larger number makes the clips taller. If the keyguard stands above the front of the case, the clips grow by that much as well.
settings.picture: 10 vs 20, with generate = horizontal clip

settings.name: case_corner_radius
settings.tip: The radius of the case's outer corners, in millimeters. It's used only when a sloped keyguard edge is extended to the edge of the case.
settings.when: Enter it when add sloped keyguard edge and extend lip to edge of case, in Sloped Keyguard Edge Info, are both yes.
settings.picture: 5 vs 20, with add sloped keyguard edge = yes and extend lip to edge of case = yes

settings.name: case_to_screen_depth
settings.tip: How far the screen sits below the front surface of the case, in millimeters. It's used for Clip-on Straps and for a sloped keyguard edge.
settings.when: Measure it when you mount with Clip-on Straps or add a sloped keyguard edge; otherwise it has no effect.
settings.values: When it's more than keyguard thickness, Clip-on Straps get raised pedestals so the clips meet the keyguard at the front of the case. A sloped edge with Clip-on Straps needs a keyguard thickness at least this deep, or the clip grooves are left off.
settings.picture: 2 vs 8, with mounting method = Clip-on Straps and keyguard thickness = 4 (pedestals appear at 8)
settings.drafter_notes: When a sloped edge is combined with Clip-on Straps and the keyguard is too thin, the grooves and pedestals are dropped with no Console message that I could find (line 1511).

settings.name: top_edge_compensation_for_tight_cases
settings.shown_as: top edge compensation for tight cases
settings.tip: The width of solid plastic along the keyguard's top edge, in millimeters, measured in from that edge. Use it when the case fits so close to the screen that the top border is too thin.
settings.when: Use it when the case opening hugs the screen and the keyguard's top border comes out thin and fragile.
settings.values: It only has an effect when it's wider than the gap between the case opening and the screen. The extra plastic comes out of whatever runs along that edge, such as a bar opening or the top row of cells, which come out slightly smaller. It needs have a case set to yes.
settings.picture: 0 vs 6, with height of opening in case = 158, upper message bar height = 20 and expose upper message bar = yes (the bar opening starts lower)
settings.question: The Handling Tight Fitting Cases page says the extra plastic is measured in from the edge of the screen; the designer measures it in from the keyguard's own edge. The draft follows the designer. Which is intended? (The same goes for the bottom, left and right ones.)
settings.drafter_notes: The Handling Tight Fitting Cases page (656) says the thickness is added from the edge of the screen inward; by the code the number is measured from the keyguard's own edge, and only the part beyond the gap to the screen is added. The Clip-on Straps page (438) still names the old 'height compensation for tight cases' and 'width compensation for tight cases' settings.

settings.name: bottom_edge_compensation_for_tight_cases
settings.shown_as: bottom edge compensation for tight cases
settings.tip: The width of solid plastic along the keyguard's bottom edge, in millimeters, measured in from that edge. Use it when the case fits so close to the screen that the bottom border is too thin.
settings.when: Use it when the case opening hugs the screen and the keyguard's bottom border comes out thin and fragile.
settings.values: It only has an effect when it's wider than the gap between the case opening and the screen. The extra plastic comes out of whatever runs along that edge, such as a bar opening or the bottom row of cells, which come out slightly smaller. It needs have a case set to yes.
settings.picture: 0 vs 6, with height of opening in case = 158, lower command bar height = 20 and expose lower command bar = yes (the bar opening ends higher)
settings.drafter_notes: Same as top edge compensation: page 656 says the thickness is added from the edge of the screen inward, while the code measures it from the keyguard's own edge.

settings.name: left_edge_compensation_for_tight_cases
settings.shown_as: left edge compensation for tight cases
settings.tip: The width of solid plastic along the keyguard's left edge, in millimeters, measured in from that edge. Use it when the case fits so close to the screen that the left border is too thin.
settings.when: Use it when the case opening hugs the screen and the keyguard's left border comes out thin and fragile.
settings.values: It only has an effect when it's wider than the gap between the case opening and the screen. The extra plastic comes out of whatever runs along that edge, such as the ends of the bar openings or the left column of cells, which come out slightly narrower. It needs have a case set to yes.
settings.picture: 0 vs 6, with width of opening in case = 210, upper message bar height = 20 and expose upper message bar = yes (the bar opening starts farther right)
settings.drafter_notes: Same as top edge compensation: page 656 says the thickness is added from the edge of the screen inward, while the code measures it from the keyguard's own edge. With Posts mounting, the posts on this side also get longer by this amount (lines 2864-2866).

settings.name: right_edge_compensation_for_tight_cases
settings.shown_as: right edge compensation for tight cases
settings.tip: The width of solid plastic along the keyguard's right edge, in millimeters, measured in from that edge. Use it when the case fits so close to the screen that the right border is too thin.
settings.when: Use it when the case opening hugs the screen and the keyguard's right border comes out thin and fragile.
settings.values: It only has an effect when it's wider than the gap between the case opening and the screen. The extra plastic comes out of whatever runs along that edge, such as the ends of the bar openings or the right column of cells, which come out slightly narrower. It needs have a case set to yes.
settings.picture: 0 vs 6, with width of opening in case = 210, upper message bar height = 20 and expose upper message bar = yes (the bar opening ends farther left)
settings.drafter_notes: Same as top edge compensation: page 656 says the thickness is added from the edge of the screen inward, while the code measures it from the keyguard's own edge. With Posts mounting, the posts on this side also get longer by this amount (lines 2864-2866).

settings.name: bottom_of_status_bar
settings.tip: Where the bottom edge of the status bar falls, in pixels from the top edge of your screenshot. Enter 0 if the screenshot shows no status bar.
settings.when: Use this section instead of App Layout in mm whenever you have a screenshot of the app; it's more accurate than measuring the screen with a ruler.
settings.values: The five settings here are positions read off the screenshot in a graphics program, not heights. Any number above 0 in this section makes the designer use it and ignore App Layout in mm.
settings.picture: 0 vs 150, with expose status bar = yes and both top of lower message bar and top of lower command bar = 1620 (the screenshot height for iPad 9th generation in landscape)
settings.drafter_notes: The code also accepts the five positions measured up from the bottom of the screenshot: it decides which way by comparing this setting with top of lower command bar (line 1219). That is why leaving top of lower command bar at 0 breaks the layout. The User Manual's section 4.3 says to enter 'the height of each bar' in either section; in this section they are positions, not heights.

settings.name: bottom_of_upper_message_bar
settings.tip: Where the bottom edge of the upper message bar, which shows what has been said, falls in pixels from the top edge of your screenshot.
settings.when: Enter it when the app has a message bar near the top of the screen.
settings.values: If the app has no upper message bar, enter the same number as bottom of status bar. Left at 0, the status bar is counted twice when there's an upper command bar below it.
settings.picture: 60 vs 300, with bottom of status bar = 60, expose upper message bar = yes, and both top of lower message bar and top of lower command bar = 1620

settings.name: bottom_of_upper_command_bar
settings.tip: Where the bottom edge of the upper command bar, the row of app controls below the upper message bar, falls in pixels from the top edge of your screenshot.
settings.when: Enter it when the app has a bar of controls below its upper message bar.
settings.values: If the app has no upper command bar, enter the same number as the bar above it.
settings.picture: 300 vs 420, with bottom of status bar = 60, bottom of upper message bar = 300, expose upper command bar = yes, and both top of lower message bar and top of lower command bar = 1620

settings.name: top_of_lower_message_bar
settings.tip: Where the top edge of a message bar near the bottom of the screen falls, in pixels from the top edge of your screenshot.
settings.when: Enter it when the app has a message bar near the bottom of the screen.
settings.values: If there's no lower message bar, enter the same number as top of lower command bar. If the app has neither lower bar, enter the screenshot's full height in pixels in both (1620 for an iPad 9th generation in landscape).
settings.picture: 1620 vs 1400, with top of lower command bar = 1620 and expose lower message bar = yes

settings.name: top_of_lower_command_bar
settings.tip: Where the top edge of a command bar along the bottom of the screen falls, in pixels from the top edge of your screenshot.
settings.when: Fill it in whenever you use this section: the bar's top edge, or the screenshot's full height if the app has no lower command bar.
settings.values: With no lower command bar, enter the screenshot's full height in pixels (1620 for an iPad 9th generation in landscape; the Tablet Pixel Dimensions page lists others). Left at 0, the designer reads all five numbers as measured from the bottom of the screenshot and the layout comes out wrong.
settings.picture: 1620 vs 1450, with top of lower message bar set to the same number each time and expose lower command bar = yes
settings.drafter_notes: That a 0 here turns the whole section to bottom-up measuring is my reading of line 1219; I didn't render it to see what the result looks like.

settings.name: status_bar_height
settings.tip: The height of the status bar across the top of the screen, which shows the time and battery, in millimeters.
settings.when: Enter it when you've measured the app on the tablet with a ruler and the screen shows a status bar.
settings.values: Ignored when any setting in App Layout in px is above 0. The grid fills the height the bars leave.
settings.picture: 0 vs 15, with expose status bar = yes

settings.name: upper_message_bar_height
settings.tip: The height of the message bar below the status bar, which shows what has been said, in millimeters.
settings.when: Enter it when the app has a message bar near the top and you've measured it with a ruler.
settings.values: Ignored when any setting in App Layout in px is above 0. The grid fills the height the bars leave.
settings.picture: 0 vs 20, with expose upper message bar = yes

settings.name: upper_command_bar_height
settings.tip: The height of the bar of app controls below the upper message bar, in millimeters.
settings.when: Enter it when the app has a bar of controls near the top and you've measured it with a ruler.
settings.values: Ignored when any setting in App Layout in px is above 0. The grid fills the height the bars leave.
settings.picture: 0 vs 15, with expose upper command bar = yes

settings.name: lower_message_bar_height
settings.tip: The height of a message bar near the bottom of the screen, directly above any lower command bar, in millimeters.
settings.when: Enter it when the app has a message bar near the bottom and you've measured it with a ruler.
settings.values: Ignored when any setting in App Layout in px is above 0. The grid fills the height the bars leave.
settings.picture: 0 vs 20, with expose lower message bar = yes

settings.name: lower_command_bar_height
settings.tip: The height of a bar of app controls along the bottom edge of the screen, in millimeters.
settings.when: Enter it when the app has a bar of controls along the bottom and you've measured it with a ruler.
settings.values: Ignored when any setting in App Layout in px is above 0. The grid fills the height the bars leave.
settings.picture: 0 vs 15, with expose lower command bar = yes

settings.name: keyguard_inset_mode
settings.tip: Yes when the app has been shrunk to sit inside an equal border on the left and right and an equal border on the top and bottom. The grid and bars are then fitted to the app.
settings.when: Turn it on when the AAC app doesn't fill the screen but sits centered inside a border, then enter the border sizes below.
settings.values: It has no effect until a left or bottom inset size is above 0. The camera, the home button, the keyguard's fit in the case and the screenshot still use the whole screen, and pixel measurements are still taken from the corner of the full screenshot.
settings.note: the app has been shrunk to leave an equal border on the left/right and an equal border on the top/bottom of the screen
settings.picture: no vs yes, with left inset size in mm = 15 and bottom inset size in mm = 10 (the grid shrinks into the app)
settings.source: keyguard.scad 216, 1138-1161, 1185-1188, 1240-1255; keyguard designer CHANGELOG.md (Keyguard Inset Info entry)

settings.name: left_inset_size_in_px
settings.tip: The width of the border to the left of the app, in pixels, measured on your screenshot. The border on the right is taken to be the same.
settings.when: Enter it in keyguard inset mode when you're working from a screenshot.
settings.values: Ignored when left inset size in mm is above 0, or when keyguard inset mode is no.
settings.picture: 0 vs 150, with keyguard inset mode = yes

settings.name: bottom_inset_size_in_px
settings.tip: The height of the border below the app, in pixels, measured on your screenshot. The border above the app is taken to be the same.
settings.when: Enter it in keyguard inset mode when you're working from a screenshot.
settings.values: Ignored when bottom inset size in mm is above 0, or when keyguard inset mode is no.
settings.picture: 0 vs 120, with keyguard inset mode = yes

settings.name: left_inset_size_in_mm
settings.tip: The width of the border to the left of the app, in millimeters, measured on the screen. The border on the right is taken to be the same.
settings.when: Enter it in keyguard inset mode when you measure the border on the tablet with a ruler.
settings.values: When it's above 0 it's used instead of left inset size in px. Ignored when keyguard inset mode is no.
settings.picture: 0 vs 15, with keyguard inset mode = yes

settings.name: bottom_inset_size_in_mm
settings.tip: The height of the border below the app, in millimeters, measured on the screen. The border above the app is taken to be the same.
settings.when: Enter it in keyguard inset mode when you measure the border on the tablet with a ruler.
settings.values: When it's above 0 it's used instead of bottom inset size in px. Ignored when keyguard inset mode is no.
settings.picture: 0 vs 10, with keyguard inset mode = yes

settings.name: hide_app_region
settings.tip: Yes removes the whole app area from the keyguard, leaving only what's outside it: the border around the app and the keyguard's edge.
settings.when: Use it for a quick, open test print that checks the outline and the border around the app before you print the full keyguard.
settings.values: Without keyguard inset mode the app fills the screen, so this removes the same area as hide screen region. It applies to a keyguard frame too.
settings.picture: no vs yes, with keyguard inset mode = yes, left inset size in mm = 15 and bottom inset size in mm = 10
settings.question: What is this for? Nothing documents it. The draft assumes it's like hide screen region: a quick test print of the border around a shrunk app.
settings.drafter_notes: Why a clinician would use it isn't documented anywhere I could find; the test-print use is by analogy with the way page 358 uses hide screen region.

settings.name: expose_status_bar
settings.tip: Yes cuts a full-width opening over the status bar along the top of the screen, using its height from App Layout. An exposed bar beside it opens together with it.
settings.when: Leave it at no unless the student needs to see or touch the status bar.
settings.picture: no vs yes, with status bar height = 5 (App Layout in mm)
settings.drafter_notes: Code fact the tip leaves out: bar openings are cut only when the grid has at least one row and one column (lines 2271, 2473, 2650), so with number of rows or number of columns at 0 this setting does nothing. Also, with Posts mounting, exposing this bar (or the upper message bar) changes the single post across the top into a short post on each side (lines 2859, 2878; changelog: round post all the way across the top only if both the status bar and the upper message bar are hidden).

settings.name: expose_upper_message_bar
settings.tip: Yes cuts a full-width opening over the upper message bar, using its height from App Layout, so the student can see what has been said and tap the bar.
settings.when: Set it to yes when the student should see the message as it is built or tap the bar to speak it, which is the usual choice.
settings.picture: no vs yes, with upper message bar height = 20 (App Layout in mm)
settings.drafter_notes: Code fact the tip leaves out: bar openings are cut only when the grid has at least one row and one column (lines 2271, 2473, 2650), so with number of rows or number of columns at 0 this setting does nothing. Also, with Posts mounting, exposing this bar (or the status bar) changes the single post across the top into a short post on each side (lines 2859, 2878; changelog: round post all the way across the top only if both the status bar and the upper message bar are hidden). 'Tap the bar' assumes the app speaks when its message bar is tapped, as the manual (4.3) says most do.

settings.name: expose_upper_command_bar
settings.tip: Yes cuts a full-width opening over the upper command bar, the strip of app controls directly above the grid, using its height from App Layout.
settings.when: Set it to yes when the student needs the controls in that bar; leave it at no to keep them from being pressed by accident.
settings.picture: no vs yes, with upper command bar height = 15 (App Layout in mm)
settings.drafter_notes: Code fact the tip leaves out: bar openings are cut only when the grid has at least one row and one column (lines 2271, 2473, 2650), so with number of rows or number of columns at 0 this setting does nothing.
settings.source: keyguard.scad 227, 1270-1272 (bar order: status, upper message, upper command, then grid), 3813-3846 (bars()), 2271

settings.name: expose_lower_message_bar
settings.tip: Yes cuts a full-width opening over the lower message bar, directly below the grid, using its height from App Layout. An exposed lower command bar opens together with it.
settings.when: Set it to yes when the app shows its message below the grid and the student should see or tap it.
settings.picture: no vs yes, with lower message bar height = 15 (App Layout in mm)
settings.drafter_notes: Code fact the tip leaves out: bar openings are cut only when the grid has at least one row and one column (lines 2271, 2473, 2650), so with number of rows or number of columns at 0 this setting does nothing.
settings.source: keyguard.scad 228, 1273-1275 (lower bar order: grid, lower message, lower command), 3849-3862 (bars()), 2271

settings.name: expose_lower_command_bar
settings.tip: Yes cuts a full-width opening over the lower command bar, the strip of app controls along the bottom of the screen, using its height from App Layout.
settings.when: Set it to yes when the student needs the controls along the bottom of the app.
settings.picture: no vs yes, with lower command bar height = 15 (App Layout in mm)
settings.drafter_notes: Code fact the tip leaves out: bar openings are cut only when the grid has at least one row and one column (lines 2271, 2473, 2650), so with number of rows or number of columns at 0 this setting does nothing.

settings.name: bar_edge_slope
settings.tip: Slope, in degrees, of one edge of an exposed message bar: the edge next to its covered command bar. 90 is a straight wall; less leans it back, so the bar is easier to see and reach.
settings.when: Lower it when an exposed message bar is narrow or the keyguard is thick, so the student can see into the bar and reach it more easily.
settings.values: 90 is a straight wall. A smaller number gives a gentler slope that widens the opening at the keyguard's top surface into the covered command bar next to it, so that bar must be tall enough or the slope starts to cut into the grid's top rail (upper bar) or the keyguard's bottom border (lower bar). It applies only while that command bar is not exposed, and is ignored for laser-cut keyguards.
settings.picture: 90 vs 45, with expose upper message bar = yes, expose upper command bar = no, upper message bar height = 20 and upper command bar height = 15 (App Layout in mm), 3D-Printed; best seen from an angle or in cross-section
settings.question: The page on bar edges says a command bar's edge can be sloped too, but the designer slopes only a message bar's edge next to a covered command bar. Which is intended? The draft follows the designer.
settings.drafter_notes: Page 683 says the top edge of the upper and lower command bars can also be sloped. In the code only the message bar's edge next to a covered command bar is sloped (upper message bar's bottom edge, lower message bar's bottom edge); every command bar opening is cut at 90 degrees. The code applies the slope even when the command bar's height is 0. No range is set, so numbers above 90 are accepted; I did not check what they produce (the cutter would undercut).
settings.source: keyguard.scad 230, 606 (laser-cut forces 90), 3808-3810, 3823-3825, 3849-3851 (only places it is used), 6307 (slope order top, bottom, left, right), 4914-4945 (cut(): base size at screen, wider at top); page 683

settings.name: bar_corner_radius
settings.tip: Rounds the corners of each bar opening, in millimeters. 0 gives square corners; the radius can't be more than half the bar's height.
settings.when: Change it to match the rounding of the app's bars, or set it to 0 for square corners.
settings.values: 0 gives square corners; larger numbers round them more, up to half the height of the bar opening, beyond which nothing changes. The same radius also rounds the corners of the lowered screen area when screen area thickness is less than keyguard thickness.
settings.picture: 0 vs 8, with expose upper message bar = yes and upper message bar height = 20 (App Layout in mm)
settings.drafter_notes: The second effect (corners of the lowered screen area) comes from line 2267, where the recess cutter's corner is this radius plus half the cell edge chamfer; confirm Ken wants it in the reference.
settings.source: keyguard.scad 231, 1309, 2267, 3806-3861 (every bar cut), 4694 (radius capped at half the opening's smaller side); changelog: limit the bar corner radius for thin bars

settings.name: number_of_rows
settings.tip: How many rows of buttons the app's grid has. Set it to 0 for a keyguard with no grid, such as one for a free-form app.
settings.when: Set it to match the page of the app the keyguard is for.
settings.values: Each row gets an equal share of the grid's height, with the cell centered in it. 0 removes the grid, and with it any bar openings from Bar Info; openings then come from Custom Openings or the openings-and-additions file. If the rows don't fit at the cell height you set, the cells are made smaller and the Console says so.
settings.picture: 3 vs 5
settings.question: With 0 rows or 0 columns, the designer cuts no bar openings either, so a free-form keyguard can't open a bar from Bar Info. Is that intended?
settings.drafter_notes: Code fact: with 0 rows or 0 columns the bar openings from Bar Info are not cut either (lines 2271, 2473), and hide grid region does nothing; I put this in values. Confirm it is intended.

settings.name: number_of_columns
settings.tip: How many columns of buttons the app's grid has. Set it to 0 for a keyguard with no grid, such as one for a free-form app.
settings.when: Set it to match the page of the app the keyguard is for.
settings.values: Each column gets an equal share of the grid's width, with the cell centered in it. 0 removes the grid, and with it any bar openings from Bar Info. If the columns don't fit at the cell width you set, the cells are made narrower and the Console says so.
settings.picture: 4 vs 6
settings.drafter_notes: Code fact: with 0 rows or 0 columns the bar openings from Bar Info are not cut either (lines 2271, 2473), and hide grid region does nothing; I put this in values. Confirm it is intended.

settings.name: cell_shape
settings.tip: Whether each cell opening is a rectangle or a circle. A circle is centered over each button and sized by cell diameter; a rectangle uses the cell height, width and corner radius.
settings.when: Choose circular when you want a round opening centered on each button instead of one shaped like the button.
settings.values: rectangular: sized by cell height and cell width (in millimeters, or in pixels when the millimeter value is 0), with cell corner radius. circular: a round opening of cell diameter; cell height and width are not used for the openings, and circular cells are not shrunk to fit.
settings.picture: rectangular vs circular
settings.drafter_notes: Merging still works on circular cells: the code cuts a straight band between them, which should give a slot-shaped opening (not rendered to confirm). Ridges around merged circular cells are drawn as separate rings, not one wall around the group (code comment: merging is not supported for circular cells).

settings.name: cell_height_in_px
settings.tip: Height of each rectangular cell opening, in pixels as measured on a screenshot. Used only when cell height in mm is 0.
settings.when: Use it when you measured the buttons on a screenshot; set cell height in mm to 0 first.
settings.values: The tablet's pixel size turns it into millimeters. If the rows don't fit in the grid at this height, the cells are made shorter and the Console gives the height actually used.
settings.picture: 100 vs 200, with cell height in mm = 0
settings.drafter_notes: At the default, cell height in mm is 25, so this setting does nothing until that is set to 0; the Beginner level hides this setting but shows the mm one.
settings.source: keyguard.scad 238, 1372, 1374, 1376-1380; skill-config.txt 88; changelog: Added support for specifying cell height and width in pixels

settings.name: cell_width_in_px
settings.tip: Width of each rectangular cell opening, in pixels as measured on a screenshot. Used only when cell width in mm is 0.
settings.when: Use it when you measured the buttons on a screenshot; set cell width in mm to 0 first.
settings.values: The tablet's pixel size turns it into millimeters. If the columns don't fit in the grid at this width, the cells are made narrower and the Console gives the width actually used.
settings.picture: 150 vs 250, with cell width in mm = 0
settings.drafter_notes: At the default, cell width in mm is 25, so this setting does nothing until that is set to 0; the Beginner level hides this setting but shows the mm one.

settings.name: cell_height_in_mm
settings.tip: Height of each rectangular cell opening, in millimeters. Set it to 0 to give the height in pixels with cell height in px instead.
settings.when: Set it from the height of the app's buttons, measured on the tablet.
settings.values: If the rows don't fit in the grid at this height, the cells are made shorter and the Console gives the height actually used. Not used when cell shape is circular.

settings.name: cell_width_in_mm
settings.tip: Width of each rectangular cell opening, in millimeters. Set it to 0 to give the width in pixels with cell width in px instead.
settings.when: Set it from the width of the app's buttons, measured on the tablet.
settings.values: If the columns don't fit in the grid at this width, the cells are made narrower and the Console gives the width actually used. Not used when cell shape is circular.

settings.name: cell_corner_radius
settings.tip: Rounds the corners of rectangular cell openings, in millimeters. 0 gives square corners; half the cell's shorter side gives fully rounded ends.
settings.when: Change it to match the rounding of the app's buttons.
settings.values: Anything above half the cell's shorter side has no further effect. On a laser-cut keyguard with Laser Cutting best practices on, the corners are rounded by at least a tenth of the cell's shorter side. It also sets the corners of cell inserts and the rounding of ridges around merged cells.
settings.picture: 0 vs 10
settings.source: keyguard.scad 242, 1389, 1394-1397 (cap and laser-cut minimum), 3944-3948, 3971, 4289-4290 (merged ridges), 5051, 5076 (cell inserts)

settings.name: cell_diameter
settings.tip: Diameter of each circular cell opening, in millimeters. Used only when cell shape is circular.
settings.when: Set it to the size of round opening you want over each button.
settings.values: Unlike rectangular cells, circular cells are not shrunk to fit, so a diameter larger than a cell's share of the grid makes neighboring openings run together.
settings.picture: 10 vs 25, with cell shape = circular
settings.drafter_notes: 'Run together' is from reading the code (no fit check for circular cells, line 1376; cut at full diameter, line 3950), not from a render.

settings.name: cell_edge_slope
settings.tip: Slope, in degrees, of the walls of every cell opening. 90 is a straight wall; less leans the walls back, so each opening is wider at the top and easier to see into and reach.
settings.when: Lower it, 60 being a common choice, when the student has trouble seeing or reaching the buttons at the bottom of deep openings.
settings.values: The opening keeps its set size at the screen and grows at the keyguard's top surface, so the rails get narrower on top; the thicker the screen area, the more it grows. cell top edge slope and cell bottom edge slope, when not 90, replace it for those edges. Ignored for laser-cut keyguards.
settings.picture: 90 vs 60, 3D-Printed; best seen from an angle or in cross-section
settings.source: keyguard.scad 247, 604, 1412-1417, 3929-3950, 4914-4945 (cut(): base at screen, wider at top), 6348 (comment: 60 is the dominant pattern in real designs); page 3469

settings.name: cover_these_cells
settings.tip: Cells to leave covered with plastic, so those buttons can't be pressed. Cells are numbered left to right, starting with the bottom row.
settings.when: Use it to block buttons the student shouldn't press, or places in the grid where the app has no button.
settings.values: Separate the cell numbers with commas. In a 3-row, 4-column grid, cells 1 to 4 are the bottom row and 9 to 12 the top row.
settings.note: example: 3,6,12
settings.picture: empty vs 2,7 (in the default 3 by 4 grid)
settings.drafter_notes: If a covered cell is the second cell of a merge, the merge still opens the band reaching to that cell's center; an edge case, not rendered.

settings.name: merge_cells_horizontally_starting_at
settings.tip: Cells to join to the cell on their right, removing the rail between them. Cells are numbered left to right, starting with the bottom row.
settings.when: Use it when one of the app's buttons spans two or more grid cells across.
settings.values: To join three cells in a row, list the first two: 5,6 joins 5, 6 and 7. A cell in the right-hand column has nothing to its right, so listing it does nothing.
settings.note: example: 5,8 merges cells 5&6 and 8&9
settings.picture: empty vs 5,6 (in the default 3 by 4 grid)
settings.drafter_notes: Also applies to circular cells, as a straight band between them; see cell shape.
settings.source: keyguard.scad 251, 887, 3902, 3927-3930, 3953-3999 (rounded inner corners of L-shapes); page 7995

settings.name: merge_cells_vertically_starting_at
settings.tip: Cells to join to the cell above them, removing the rail between them. Cells are numbered left to right, starting with the bottom row.
settings.when: Use it when one of the app's buttons spans two or more grid cells up and down.
settings.values: To join three cells in a column, list the lower two: in a 4-column grid, 2,6 joins 2, 6 and 10. A cell in the top row has nothing above it, so listing it does nothing. Used with merge cells horizontally starting at, it makes L-shaped and larger openings.
settings.note: example: 3,4 merges cell 3 and the cell above and cell 4 and the cell above
settings.picture: empty vs 2,6 (in the default 3 by 4 grid)

settings.name: add_a_ridge_around_these_cells
settings.shown_as: add a ridge around these cells
settings.tip: Cells to get a raised wall around their opening, so the student can find them by touch. Listing any cell of a merged group walls the whole group. 3D-printed only.
settings.when: Use it to help a student with a visual impairment find particular buttons by touch.
settings.values: The wall stands on the rail outside the opening, so the opening keeps its full size. Its height and thickness come from height of ridge and thickness of ridge. Cells are numbered as for cover these cells.
settings.note: example: 3,6,12
settings.picture: empty vs 6, 3D-Printed
settings.drafter_notes: Ignored on laser-cut keyguards (line 2347). For circular cells each listed cell gets its own ring, even if merged.
settings.source: keyguard.scad 255, 889, 2347-2349, 4151-4220 (cell_ridges), 4182-4185 (one ridge per merged group); pages 21977, 3469

settings.name: height_of_ridge
settings.tip: How far the ridges around cells rise above the surface of the grid, in millimeters.
settings.when: Raise it if the student has trouble feeling the ridges; lower it if they get in the way of the student's hand.
settings.values: Measured from the top of the grid area, which sits lower than the rest of the keyguard when screen area thickness is less than keyguard thickness.
settings.picture: 1 vs 4, with add a ridge around these cells = 6, 3D-Printed
settings.drafter_notes: It also supplies a ridge-height value that the openings-and-additions file can use (line 1391), given in pixels when unit of measure for screen is px; not mentioned in the tip.
settings.source: keyguard.scad 256, 1391, 4158-4161 (wall top = grid surface + this height), 4201, 4217, 4382-4403, 4588-4597

settings.name: thickness_of_ridge
settings.tip: How thick the walls of the ridges around cells are, in millimeters. The wall stands on the rail, outside the opening, so the opening keeps its size.
settings.when: Change it for a sturdier or a slimmer ridge, keeping it narrower than the rails it stands on.
settings.values: A thicker wall is sturdier and easier to feel but covers more of the rail; where two ridged cells sit side by side, walls thicker than half the rail between them run together.
settings.picture: 1 vs 4, with add a ridge around these cells = 6, 3D-Printed
settings.drafter_notes: 'Run together' is from the geometry (each wall grows outward from its own opening), not from a render. It also supplies a ridge-thickness value for the openings-and-additions file (line 1392).
settings.source: keyguard.scad 257, 1392, 3960-3971, 4196-4201 (wall grows outward, opening keeps its size), 4217, 4289

settings.name: cell_top_edge_slope
settings.tip: Slope, in degrees, of the top wall of every cell opening. At 90 it follows cell edge slope; any other number sets the top wall on its own.
settings.when: Change it when the student looks at the tablet from a steep or shallow angle and the top wall of each opening hides part of the button.
settings.values: A smaller number leans the top wall back. Because 90 means 'same as cell edge slope', the top wall can't be made straight while the other walls are sloped. Ignored for laser-cut keyguards.
settings.picture: 90 vs 45, with cell edge slope = 90, 3D-Printed; best seen from an angle or in cross-section
settings.source: keyguard.scad 258, 1412-1413, 3929-3950; changelog: change the slopes of the top and bottom edges of cell openings to provide added visibility when looking at tablet at small or very large angle

settings.name: cell_bottom_edge_slope
settings.tip: Slope, in degrees, of the bottom wall of every cell opening. At 90 it follows cell edge slope; any other number sets the bottom wall on its own.
settings.when: Change it when the student looks at the tablet from a steep or shallow angle and the bottom wall of each opening hides part of the button.
settings.values: A smaller number leans the bottom wall back. Because 90 means 'same as cell edge slope', the bottom wall can't be made straight while the other walls are sloped. Ignored for laser-cut keyguards.
settings.picture: 90 vs 45, with cell edge slope = 90, 3D-Printed; best seen from an angle or in cross-section
settings.source: keyguard.scad 259, 1414-1415, 3929-3950; same changelog entry as cell top edge slope

settings.name: top_padding
settings.tip: Extra space, in millimeters, between the top of the grid and the bars or screen edge above it. The rows are spread evenly over what's left.
settings.when: Use it when the grid rails don't line up with the app's buttons because the app leaves more space above its top row than half the space between its buttons.
settings.values: Every row moves down, the top row the most. The cells keep their size and the rails between them get narrower; if the cells no longer fit, they are made smaller. A negative number pushes that side of the grid outward instead.
settings.picture: 0 vs 20
settings.source: keyguard.scad 260, 1313, 1374, 1384, 3896-3904; changelog: Added support for negative padding values; page 560

settings.name: bottom_padding
settings.tip: Extra space, in millimeters, between the bottom of the grid and the bars or screen edge below it. The rows are spread evenly over what's left.
settings.when: Use it when the grid rails don't line up with the app's buttons because the app leaves more space below its bottom row than half the space between its buttons.
settings.values: Every row moves up, the bottom row the most. The cells keep their size and the rails between them get narrower; if the cells no longer fit, they are made smaller. A negative number pushes that side of the grid outward instead.
settings.picture: 0 vs 20

settings.name: left_padding
settings.tip: Extra space, in millimeters, between the left edge of the screen and the grid. The columns are spread evenly over what's left.
settings.when: Use it when the grid rails don't line up with the app's buttons because the app leaves more space to the left of its first column than half the space between its buttons.
settings.values: Every column moves right, the left column the most. The cells keep their size and the rails between them get narrower; if the cells no longer fit, they are made smaller. A negative number pushes that side of the grid outward instead.
settings.picture: 0 vs 20
settings.drafter_notes: In keyguard inset mode it is measured from the app's left edge, not the screen's (grid starts at the app's edge, line 1315).

settings.name: right_padding
settings.tip: Extra space, in millimeters, between the grid and the right edge of the screen. The columns are spread evenly over what's left.
settings.when: Use it when the grid rails don't line up with the app's buttons because the app leaves extra space on the right, or to leave a narrower last column out of the grid and open it with Custom Openings instead.
settings.values: Every column moves left, the right column the most. The cells keep their size and the rails between them get narrower; if the cells no longer fit, they are made smaller. A negative number pushes that side of the grid outward instead.
settings.picture: 0 vs 20
settings.drafter_notes: In keyguard inset mode it is measured from the app's right edge. The narrower-last-column use is the VocoChat example on page 560, which uses the openings-and-additions file; I named Custom Openings as the app's way to do it.

settings.name: hide_grid_region
settings.tip: Yes cuts away the whole grid area, cells and rails, leaving the bars and border. With the screenshot shown, it lets you see the app's buttons while you set the padding.
settings.when: Turn it on for a while, with include screenshot set to yes, to see where the app's buttons fall as you set the padding, then set it back to no for the finished keyguard.
settings.values: It removes everything inside the grid area, including any ridges or custom openings there. It does nothing when number of rows or number of columns is 0.
settings.picture: no vs yes
settings.question: Is this only an aid while you set the padding (the draft tells clinicians to set it back to no), or do you also use it in finished keyguards?
settings.drafter_notes: The only stated purpose found is the changelog's 'to help with setting padding values based on a screenshot'. I assumed it is a temporary aid and wrote 'set it back to no'; if Ken uses it in finished designs, drop that part.
settings.source: keyguard.scad 264, 548, 2396-2398, 2555-2557, 2771-2773, 8456-8468 (cut_grid, gated on rows and columns); changelog versions 83, 85, 89

settings.name: mounting_method
settings.tip: How the keyguard is held on. Suction Cups, Velcro and Screw-on Straps are for a tablet without a case; Posts, Shelf and both kinds of tabs need a case. Clip-on Straps work either way.
settings.when: Choose it once you know whether the tablet will be in a case and how firmly the keyguard needs to stay in place.
settings.values: - none - adds nothing: the keyguard is squeezed into a soft case opening or held on with micro-suction tape. Suction Cups cuts holes in the tablet border, left and right of the screen, for four small suction cups. Velcro cuts four shallow recesses in the back of the keyguard for Velcro dots or squares. Screw-on Straps cuts slots and screw holes near the left and right ends for Keyguard AT's screw-on straps. Clip-on Straps cuts grooves near the edges for printed clips joined by elastic straps behind the tablet; in a case it also adds small raised blocks that bring the grooves up to the case's surface. Posts trims the top of the keyguard and adds posts sticking out of each side, which snap into a case with a built-in keyguard mount, such as PRC's Via Pro. Shelf adds a thin lip all the way around the back edge that slides under the edge of the case opening. Slide-in Tabs adds thin tabs at the back edge that slide under the edge of the case opening. Raised Tabs adds tabs that ramp up from the keyguard's edge onto the case's screen protector, held with gel tape or magnets. A laser-cut keyguard can use only - none - or Slide-in Tabs. With a keyguard frame, Shelf, Clip-on Straps and both kinds of tabs go on the frame instead of the keyguard.
settings.picture: - none - vs Slide-in Tabs; have a case = yes
settings.question: Is Posts meant to work with a keyguard frame? Today the posts are built on the keyguard inside the frame, not on the frame.
settings.drafter_notes: 1) Suction Cups, Velcro and Screw-on Straps place their cuts as if the tablet's longer side always ran left to right, so in portrait they appear to land outside the keyguard and not show. Worth checking in the app. 2) For a laser-cut keyguard with any method other than - none - or Slide-in Tabs, the 'first layer for SVG/DXF file' choice of generate makes no shape at all (Raised Tabs and Clip-on Straps show a 'not supported' message; the others show only a list of settings), while the 'keyguard' view quietly leaves the method off. Looks like a bug: that one check reads the setting before the laser-cut filter is applied. 3) With a keyguard frame, Posts are still built on the keyguard, not the frame (see post diameter).

settings.name: velcro_size
settings.tip: The size and shape of the four Velcro pads. The keyguard gets a matching round or square recess for each, 1.75 millimeters deep in its back, near the left and right edges.
settings.when: Change it to match the Velcro dots or squares you have; it is used only when mounting method is Velcro and the tablet has no case.
settings.values: Dots make round recesses and squares make square ones. The three sizes are cut at 10, 16 and 20 millimeters across, for either shape.
settings.picture: 1 vs 6; have a case = no, mounting method = Velcro, orientation = landscape, seen from the back of the keyguard
settings.drafter_notes: The inch sizes are cut slightly large (3/8 in as 10 mm, 5/8 in as 16 mm, 3/4 in as 20 mm), presumably on purpose for clearance. In portrait the recesses may fall outside the keyguard (see mounting method).

settings.name: clip_locations
settings.tip: Which edges get clips. Horizontal clips sit on the left and right edges, vertical clips on the top and bottom edges, two clips to each edge.
settings.when: Change it when you want straps running top to bottom, alone or as well as side to side.
settings.values: horizontal only puts two clips on each of the left and right edges; vertical only puts two on each of the top and bottom edges; horizontal and vertical uses all four edges. These names refer to the edges as you see the keyguard, in either orientation. No clips are made if add sloped keyguard edge is yes and the keyguard is thinner than case to screen depth.
settings.picture: horizontal only vs horizontal and vertical; mounting method = Clip-on Straps, have a case = yes

settings.name: horizontal_clip_width
settings.tip: How wide, in millimeters, each clip on the left and right edges is, measured along the edge. The grooves in the keyguard and the horizontal clips you print both follow it.
settings.when: Change it to suit your elastic band, since the strap slot is 4 millimeters narrower than the clip, or widen it for a steadier grip on a tight case.
settings.values: The groove cut for each clip is 2 millimeters wider than the clip; in a case, the raised block it hooks onto is 10 millimeters wider.
settings.picture: 20 vs 35; mounting method = Clip-on Straps, have a case = yes, clip locations = horizontal only

settings.name: vertical_clip_width
settings.tip: How wide, in millimeters, each clip on the top and bottom edges is, measured along the edge. The grooves in the keyguard and the vertical clips you print both follow it.
settings.when: Change it to suit your elastic band, since the strap slot is 4 millimeters narrower than the clip, or widen it for a steadier grip on a tight case.
settings.values: The groove cut for each clip is 2 millimeters wider than the clip; in a case, the raised block it hooks onto is 10 millimeters wider.
settings.picture: 20 vs 35; mounting method = Clip-on Straps, have a case = yes, clip locations = vertical only

settings.name: distance_between_horizontal_clips
settings.tip: The gap, in millimeters, between the two clips on each of the left and right edges. A larger number spreads them toward the corners.
settings.when: Change it when the clips would land on something on the case edge, such as a button or handle, or to spread them further apart.
settings.values: It is measured between the inner edges of the two grooves.
settings.picture: 20 vs 100; mounting method = Clip-on Straps, have a case = yes, clip locations = horizontal only

settings.name: distance_between_vertical_clips
settings.tip: The gap, in millimeters, between the two clips on each of the top and bottom edges. A larger number spreads them toward the corners.
settings.when: Change it when the clips would land on something on the case edge, such as a button or handle, or to spread them further apart.
settings.values: It is measured between the inner edges of the two grooves.
settings.picture: 40 vs 120; mounting method = Clip-on Straps, have a case = yes, clip locations = vertical only

settings.name: clip_bottom_length
settings.tip: How long, in millimeters, the bottom leg of a full-size clip is: the part that lies against the back of the tablet or case, with the strap slots at its far end.
settings.when: Change it to move the strap slots further onto the back of the tablet, or to make room for a silicone bumper.
settings.values: At 30 or more, the leg also gets a round recess for a 10 millimeter silicone bumper. It changes only the full-size horizontal and vertical clips; mini and micro clips have no bottom leg, and the keyguard itself is unchanged.
settings.picture: 25 vs 45; generate = horizontal clip (the bumper recess appears at 30 and above)

settings.name: post_diameter
settings.tip: The thickness of the posts, in millimeters. The bottom of each post lines up with the back of the keyguard, so a post thicker than the keyguard stands above its top surface.
settings.when: Set it to match the holes the posts snap into in the case's keyguard mount; if you have the system's own keyguard, measure its posts.
settings.values: When it equals keyguard thickness, the posts are flush with both faces of the keyguard.
settings.picture: 4 vs 6; mounting method = Posts, have a case = yes, keyguard thickness = 4, seen from the side
settings.drafter_notes: With a keyguard frame, the posts are still built on the keyguard, not the frame, and this setting is ignored for the two short side posts (the keyguard thickness is used instead) but still used for the single full-width post. Looks inconsistent; I could not tell whether Posts with a frame is meant to be used at all.

settings.name: post_length
settings.tip: How far, in millimeters, each post sticks out past the left and right edges of the case opening.
settings.when: Set it to how far the case's keyguard mount lets the posts reach in; measure the system's own keyguard if you have one.
settings.values: Normally one post runs the full width of the keyguard along its top edge and sticks out at both ends. If expose status bar or expose upper message bar is yes, it becomes two short posts, one at each side, so the bar stays open.
settings.picture: 3 vs 10; mounting method = Posts, have a case = yes

settings.name: mount_to_top_of_opening_distance
settings.shown_as: mount to top of opening distance
settings.tip: How far, in millimeters, the center of the posts sits below the top edge of the case opening. The keyguard's top edge is cut off along that same line.
settings.when: Measure it from the top edge of the case opening to the center of the spot where the posts snap in, carefully: if it's off, the bottom won't fit and the keyguard may not sit flat on the screen.
settings.values: A larger number moves the posts down and makes the keyguard shorter at the top.
settings.picture: 5 vs 20; mounting method = Posts, have a case = yes

settings.name: notch_in_post
settings.tip: Yes cuts a flat, slightly angled notch along the upper side of each post, which can make the post easier to snap into place.
settings.when: Leave it as yes if the system's own keyguard has this notch on its posts; set it to no if it doesn't.
settings.picture: no vs yes; mounting method = Posts, have a case = yes, close-up of one post end seen from the side
settings.drafter_notes: From the code, the notch faces the top of the case opening and tilts about 17 degrees toward the back of the keyguard; I worked this out from the numbers, not by looking.

settings.name: add_mini_tabs
settings.tip: Yes adds two small tabs on the bottom edge of the keyguard, one near each end, that snap into indents in the case's keyguard mount to hold the keyguard against the screen.
settings.when: Set it to yes if the case's keyguard mount has indents at the bottom for tabs, or the system's own keyguard has them.
settings.picture: no vs yes; mounting method = Posts, have a case = yes

settings.name: mini_tab_width
settings.tip: How wide, in millimeters, each mini tab is, measured along the bottom edge of the keyguard.
settings.when: Match it to the indents in the case's mount, or to the tabs on the system's own keyguard.
settings.picture: 10 vs 25; mounting method = Posts, have a case = yes, add mini tabs = yes

settings.name: mini_tab_length
settings.tip: How far, in millimeters, each mini tab sticks out past the bottom edge of the keyguard.
settings.when: Match it to how deep the indents in the case's mount are, or to the tabs on the system's own keyguard.
settings.picture: 2 vs 6; mounting method = Posts, have a case = yes, add mini tabs = yes

settings.name: mini_tab_inset_distance
settings.tip: How far, in millimeters, each mini tab sits in from its side of the case opening, measured to the tab's outer edge.
settings.when: Match it to where the indents are in the case's mount.
settings.values: A larger number moves both tabs toward the middle.
settings.picture: 20 vs 60; mounting method = Posts, have a case = yes, add mini tabs = yes

settings.name: mini_tab_height
settings.tip: How high, in millimeters, the underside of each mini tab sits above the back of the keyguard. 0 keeps the tabs flush with the back.
settings.when: Match it to the height of the indents in the case's mount.
settings.values: The tab itself is always 1 millimeter thick, and it can't be raised above keyguard thickness less 2 millimeters. Above 0 the tabs overhang, so turn on supports in your slicer.
settings.picture: 0 vs 2; mounting method = Posts, have a case = yes, add mini tabs = yes, keyguard thickness = 4, seen from the side

settings.name: rotate_mini_tab
settings.tip: Tilts the two mini tabs, in degrees, as mirror images of each other, turning each about the point where it meets the bottom edge.
settings.when: Leave it at 0 unless the indents in the case's mount are angled.
settings.values: A positive angle swings the tips outward, toward the nearer side of the keyguard; a negative angle swings them toward the middle.
settings.picture: 0 vs 30; mounting method = Posts, have a case = yes, add mini tabs = yes
settings.drafter_notes: The direction (positive swings outward, seen from the front) is worked out from the code, not checked on screen.

settings.name: shelf_thickness
settings.tip: How thick, in millimeters, the shelf is. It lies at the back of the keyguard and can't be thicker than the keyguard, or the keyguard frame if there is one.
settings.when: Make it thin enough to fit between the tablet and the edge of the case opening; if you are replacing the case's screen protector, measure that.
settings.picture: 1 vs 3; mounting method = Shelf, have a case = yes, keyguard thickness = 4, seen from the side

settings.name: shelf_depth
settings.tip: How far, in millimeters, the shelf reaches out past the edge of the case opening, on every side.
settings.when: Make it deep enough to stay under the edge of the case opening, but not so deep that it runs into other parts of the case.
settings.picture: 3 vs 10; mounting method = Shelf, have a case = yes

settings.name: shelf_corner_radius
settings.tip: How rounded, in millimeters, the corners of the shelf's outline are. It can differ from the keyguard's own corners.
settings.when: Change it when the corners under the case edge curve more or less than the keyguard's, so the shelf fits into them.
settings.values: 0 gives square corners.
settings.picture: 0 vs 15; mounting method = Shelf, have a case = yes, shelf depth = 8

settings.name: slide_in_tab_locations
settings.tip: Which edges get slide-in tabs. Horizontal tabs sit on the left and right edges, vertical tabs on the top and bottom edges, two tabs to each edge.
settings.when: Change it to put tabs on the edges where the case will let them slide under: the short ends, the long sides, or all four.
settings.values: horizontal only puts two tabs on each of the left and right edges; vertical only puts two on each of the top and bottom edges; horizontal and vertical uses all four edges. These names refer to the edges as you see the keyguard, in either orientation.
settings.picture: horizontal only vs horizontal and vertical; mounting method = Slide-in Tabs, have a case = yes
settings.drafter_notes: With a keyguard frame, the code puts the slide-in tabs at the edge of the keyguard inside the frame (keyguard width and height in Keyguard Frame Info), not at the frame's outer edge, so they may end up hidden inside the frame. The Keyguard Frame page shows them on the frame's outer edge. Raised tabs and clips use the outer edge correctly. Worth checking in the app.

settings.name: preferred_slide_in_tab_thickness
settings.tip: How thick, in millimeters, you'd like the slide-in tabs. They sit at the back of the keyguard and can be no thicker than the keyguard less 0.65 millimeters.
settings.when: Make it thin enough to slip under the edge of the case opening, and thick enough that the tabs don't break.
settings.picture: 1 vs 3; mounting method = Slide-in Tabs, have a case = yes, keyguard thickness = 4, seen from the side
settings.drafter_notes: The Slide-in Tabs page explains the limit as keeping the tab below the keyguard's 45-degree top chamfer, but the code uses a fixed 0.65 millimeters whatever keyguard edge chamfer is set to. For laser-cut keyguards the code reports a tab thickness (1 millimeter when use Laser Cutting best practices is yes), but the cut file is flat, so I could not tell how that thickness reaches the finished acrylic tab.

settings.name: horizontal_slide_in_tab_length
settings.tip: How far, in millimeters, each slide-in tab on the left and right edges reaches out past the keyguard's edge, to go under the case.
settings.when: Make it long enough to stay under the edge of the case opening, but short enough to work into place.
settings.values: For a laser-cut keyguard with use Laser Cutting best practices set to yes, the length is fixed at the acrylic's thickness, 3.175 millimeters, and this setting is ignored.
settings.picture: 4 vs 10; mounting method = Slide-in Tabs, have a case = yes, slide in tab locations = horizontal only

settings.name: vertical_slide_in_tab_length
settings.tip: How far, in millimeters, each slide-in tab on the top and bottom edges reaches out past the keyguard's edge, to go under the case.
settings.when: Make it long enough to stay under the edge of the case opening, but short enough to work into place.
settings.values: For a laser-cut keyguard with use Laser Cutting best practices set to yes, the length is fixed at the acrylic's thickness, 3.175 millimeters, and this setting is ignored.
settings.picture: 4 vs 10; mounting method = Slide-in Tabs, have a case = yes, slide in tab locations = vertical only

settings.name: horizontal_slide_in_tab_width
settings.tip: How wide, in millimeters, each slide-in tab on the left and right edges is, measured along the edge.
settings.when: Widen the tabs for a firmer hold, or narrow them to fit between things on the case edge.
settings.picture: 20 vs 40; mounting method = Slide-in Tabs, have a case = yes, slide in tab locations = horizontal only

settings.name: vertical_slide_in_tab_width
settings.tip: How wide, in millimeters, each slide-in tab on the top and bottom edges is, measured along the edge.
settings.when: Widen the tabs for a firmer hold, or narrow them to fit between things on the case edge.
settings.picture: 20 vs 40; mounting method = Slide-in Tabs, have a case = yes, slide in tab locations = vertical only

settings.name: distance_between_horizontal_slide_in_tabs
settings.shown_as: distance between horizontal slide in tabs
settings.tip: The gap, in millimeters, between the two slide-in tabs on each of the left and right edges. A negative number overlaps them into one wide tab.
settings.when: Change it to move the tabs clear of something on the case edge, or make it negative to get one long tab.
settings.values: It is measured between the inner edges of the two tabs, so a larger number spreads them toward the corners.
settings.picture: 60 vs -10; mounting method = Slide-in Tabs, have a case = yes, slide in tab locations = horizontal only

settings.name: distance_between_vertical_slide_in_tabs
settings.shown_as: distance between vertical slide in tabs
settings.tip: The gap, in millimeters, between the two slide-in tabs on each of the top and bottom edges. A negative number overlaps them into one wide tab.
settings.when: Change it to move the tabs clear of something on the case edge, or make it negative to get one long tab.
settings.values: It is measured between the inner edges of the two tabs, so a larger number spreads them toward the corners.
settings.picture: 60 vs -10; mounting method = Slide-in Tabs, have a case = yes, slide in tab locations = vertical only

settings.name: raised_tab_locations
settings.tip: Which edges get raised tabs. Horizontal tabs sit on the left and right edges, vertical tabs on the top and bottom edges, two tabs to each edge.
settings.when: Change it to put tabs on the edges where the case's screen protector gives them a good surface to rest on.
settings.values: horizontal only puts two tabs on each of the left and right edges; vertical only puts two on each of the top and bottom edges; horizontal and vertical uses all four edges. These names refer to the edges as you see the keyguard, in either orientation.
settings.picture: horizontal only vs horizontal and vertical; mounting method = Raised Tabs, have a case = yes

settings.name: raised_tab_height
settings.tip: The height, in millimeters, above the screen at which a raised tab stops climbing and runs flat. A tab too short to reach it is all ramp.
settings.when: Leave it as it is unless the tabs must reach past the slope of the screen protector onto a flat part; then set it to that flat part's height above the screen.
settings.values: It is measured from the back of the keyguard, which rests on the screen.
settings.picture: 3 vs 6; mounting method = Raised Tabs, have a case = yes, horizontal raised tab length = 15, seen from the side
settings.drafter_notes: When raised tabs starting height is above 0, the code's test for whether a tab gets a flat part ignores the starting height, so a tab near the cut-off can come out all ramp and end a little higher than this setting. Minor.

settings.name: horizontal_raised_tab_length
settings.tip: How far, in millimeters, each raised tab on the left and right edges reaches out past the edge of the case opening.
settings.when: Make it long enough to reach a good gripping surface on the screen protector; usually the ramp alone is enough.
settings.values: The tab climbs at the ramp angle until it reaches raised tab height, then runs flat for the rest of its length.
settings.picture: 8 vs 20; mounting method = Raised Tabs, have a case = yes, raised tab locations = horizontal only, seen from the side

settings.name: horizontal_raised_tab_width
settings.tip: How wide, in millimeters, each raised tab on the left and right edges is, measured along the edge.
settings.when: Widen it for more gripping surface, or to hold a magnet: about 10 millimeters wider than the magnet's length.
settings.picture: 20 vs 40; mounting method = Raised Tabs, have a case = yes, raised tab locations = horizontal only

settings.name: distance_between_horizontal_raised_tabs
settings.tip: The gap, in millimeters, between the two raised tabs on each of the left and right edges. A larger number spreads them toward the corners.
settings.when: Change it to move the tabs onto a good part of the screen protector, clear of anything on the case edge.
settings.values: It is measured between the inner edges of the two tabs.
settings.picture: 60 vs 20; mounting method = Raised Tabs, have a case = yes, raised tab locations = horizontal only

settings.name: vertical_raised_tab_length
settings.tip: How far, in millimeters, each raised tab on the top and bottom edges reaches out past the edge of the case opening.
settings.when: Make it long enough to reach a good gripping surface on the screen protector; usually the ramp alone is enough.
settings.values: The tab climbs at the ramp angle until it reaches raised tab height, then runs flat for the rest of its length.
settings.picture: 8 vs 20; mounting method = Raised Tabs, have a case = yes, raised tab locations = vertical only, seen from the side

settings.name: vertical_raised_tab_width
settings.tip: How wide, in millimeters, each raised tab on the top and bottom edges is, measured along the edge.
settings.when: Widen it for more gripping surface, or to hold a magnet: about 10 millimeters wider than the magnet's length.
settings.picture: 20 vs 40; mounting method = Raised Tabs, have a case = yes, raised tab locations = vertical only

settings.name: distance_between_vertical_raised_tabs
settings.tip: The gap, in millimeters, between the two raised tabs on each of the top and bottom edges. A larger number spreads them toward the corners.
settings.when: Change it to move the tabs onto a good part of the screen protector, clear of anything on the case edge.
settings.values: It is measured between the inner edges of the two tabs.
settings.picture: 60 vs 20; mounting method = Raised Tabs, have a case = yes, raised tab locations = vertical only

settings.name: preferred_raised_tab_thickness
