settings.tip: How thick, in millimeters, you'd like the raised tabs. The keyguard's thickness sets a limit, so the tabs may come out thinner.
settings.when: Thicken it if the tabs are too flimsy; it can't go past the limit the keyguard thickness sets.
settings.values: The limit gets smaller as raised tabs starting height or ramp angle grows. With embed magnets set to yes, the flat part is made at least 1 millimeter thicker than the magnet.
settings.picture: 1 vs 3; mounting method = Raised Tabs, have a case = yes, keyguard thickness = 4, seen from the side

settings.name: raised_tabs_starting_height
settings.tip: The height, in millimeters, above the screen at which each raised tab's ramp begins, at the keyguard's edge. It can't exceed the keyguard thickness less 1 millimeter.
settings.when: Set it to the screen protector's thickness where it meets the tablet face, plus 1 millimeter for the gel tape.
settings.picture: 0 vs 2; mounting method = Raised Tabs, have a case = yes, keyguard thickness = 4, seen from the side

settings.name: ramp_angle
settings.tip: The slope, in degrees, at which each raised tab climbs away from the keyguard's edge. It should match the slope of the screen protector's edge.
settings.when: Adjust it after a test fit: raise it if the tabs lift the keyguard off the screen, and lower it if much of each tab misses the gel tape.
settings.values: A larger angle makes a steeper ramp that reaches raised tab height sooner.
settings.picture: 20 vs 45; mounting method = Raised Tabs, have a case = yes, horizontal raised tab length = 15, seen from the side
settings.drafter_notes: The Raised Tabs page says to start at 20 degrees; the code's default is 30.

settings.name: embed_magnets
settings.tip: Yes adds a pocket inside each raised tab, open at one side, for a flat magnet, so the tabs can be held to the case with magnets instead of gel tape.
settings.when: Set it to yes if you'll hold the tabs with magnets; then choose the magnet with magnet size and enlarge the tabs until the magnet is covered.
settings.values: Make each tab about 10 millimeters wider than the magnet's length, then lengthen it until the pocket no longer breaks through the front, plus a couple of millimeters.
settings.picture: no vs yes; mounting method = Raised Tabs, have a case = yes, horizontal raised tab width = 30, horizontal raised tab length = 15
settings.drafter_notes: The Raised Tabs page says a red shape shows the magnet; that comes from the desktop OpenSCAD preview, and I doubt the web app shows it. The page also doesn't say what the magnets attach to on the case.

settings.name: magnet_size
settings.tip: The size of magnet the raised tabs are made to hold, in millimeters: length by width by thickness.
settings.when: Choose the size of the magnets you have; it is used only when embed magnets is yes.
settings.values: The tabs should be about 10 millimeters wider than the magnet's length: 30 for the 20 x 8 x 1.5 magnet, 50 for the 40 x 10 x 2 magnet.
settings.picture: 20 x 8 x 1.5 vs 40 x 10 x 2; mounting method = Raised Tabs, have a case = yes, embed magnets = yes, horizontal raised tab width = 50, horizontal raised tab length = 20
settings.drafter_notes: The Raised Tabs page lists the smaller magnet as 20x18x1.5; the code uses 20 x 8 x 1.5, which matches this setting's own choices.

settings.name: have_a_keyguard_frame
settings.tip: Yes makes the design two parts: a frame that fills the case opening and stays on the tablet, and a smaller keyguard that fits inside it, sized by keyguard height and keyguard width.
settings.when: Turn it on when the case opening is barely bigger than the screen (for example, to replace a screen protector), or when you want to swap keyguards quickly or flip one up out of the way.
settings.values: With yes, slide-in tabs, raised tabs, a shelf or clip-on straps from the Mounting Method section go on the frame instead of the keyguard, as do case additions, case openings and tablet openings. Make the frame itself by setting generate, in Keyguard Basics, to keyguard frame. Without a case, the frame is the size of the whole tablet.
settings.picture: no vs yes, with have a case = yes and generate = keyguard: the yes side shows the smaller keyguard with its snap-in tabs. A third view with generate = keyguard frame would show the frame.
settings.drafter_notes: Mounting Method set to Posts still adds its posts to the keyguard itself rather than the frame; I did not follow that combination further.

settings.name: keyguard_frame_thickness
settings.tip: How thick the frame is, in millimeters. The keyguard inside can't be thicker: if keyguard thickness is larger, the keyguard is made this thick instead.
settings.when: Change it to set how far the keyguard sits below the top of the frame, or, when mounting with posts, if the post slots break through the top of the frame.
settings.values: The keyguard and frame sit level at the back, so the keyguard's top is lower than the frame's top by the difference in thickness. With mount keyguard with set to posts, keep the frame thicker than the keyguard, or the post slots break through the frame's top.
settings.picture: 5 vs 8, with have a keyguard frame = yes, generate = keyguard frame and show keyguard with frame = yes, seen from an angle

settings.name: keyguard_height
settings.tip: The top-to-bottom size, in millimeters, of the keyguard that fits inside the frame, and of the opening cut in the frame for it. Used only when have a keyguard frame is yes.
settings.when: Change it to share the plastic between the frame and the keyguard: a smaller number leaves more frame above and below the keyguard, a larger number makes a bigger keyguard.
settings.values: Keep it smaller than the frame's own height (height of opening in case, when there is a case), so some frame remains above and below the keyguard.
settings.picture: 120 vs 160, with have a keyguard frame = yes, generate = keyguard frame and show keyguard with frame = yes, seen from above

settings.name: keyguard_width
settings.tip: The left-to-right size, in millimeters, of the keyguard that fits inside the frame, and of the opening cut in the frame for it. Used only when have a keyguard frame is yes.
settings.when: Change it to share the plastic between the frame and the keyguard: a smaller number leaves more frame beside the keyguard, a larger number makes a bigger keyguard.
settings.values: Keep it smaller than the frame's own width (width of opening in case, when there is a case), so some frame remains on the left and right.
settings.picture: 180 vs 230, with have a keyguard frame = yes, generate = keyguard frame and show keyguard with frame = yes, seen from above

settings.name: slide_keyguard_horizontally
settings.tip: Moves the keyguard left or right within the frame, in millimeters (positive is right). The openings stay over the same places on the screen, so this changes what the frame covers.
settings.when: Change it when you want more frame on one side than the other, such as when the screen sits off-center in the case opening.
settings.values: Positive moves the keyguard, and its opening in the frame, to the right; negative moves them to the left. The snap-in tabs or posts and the frame's matching grooves or slots move with it.
settings.note: slides the contained keyguard left/right within the frame, in mm (+ = right); openings stay registered to the screen
settings.picture: 0 vs 10, with have a keyguard frame = yes, generate = keyguard frame and show keyguard with frame = yes, seen from above
settings.question: No page describes this one, so "when you'd change it" is worked out from the designer. Is it right?
settings.drafter_notes: No page describes this setting, so the situation in 'when' is inferred from the code.

settings.name: slide_keyguard_vertically
settings.tip: Moves the keyguard up or down within the frame, in millimeters (positive is up). The openings stay over the same places on the screen, so this changes what the frame covers.
settings.when: Change it when you want more frame at the top than the bottom, or the other way round, such as when the screen sits off-center in the case opening.
settings.values: Positive moves the keyguard, and its opening in the frame, up; negative moves them down. The snap-in tabs or posts and the frame's matching grooves or slots move with it.
settings.note: slides the contained keyguard up/down within the frame, in mm (+ = up); openings stay registered to the screen
settings.picture: 0 vs 4, with have a keyguard frame = yes, generate = keyguard frame and show keyguard with frame = yes, seen from above (the default sizes leave only 5 millimeters of frame above and below the keyguard)
settings.question: No page describes this one, so "when you'd change it" is worked out from the designer. Is it right?
settings.drafter_notes: No page describes this setting, so the situation in 'when' is inferred from the code.

settings.name: keyguard_corner_radius
settings.tip: How rounded the corners of the keyguard inside the frame are, in millimeters. The frame's opening gets the same corners. Ignored when mount keyguard with is posts.
settings.when: Leave it as it is unless you want rounder or squarer corners on a keyguard that snaps into a frame.
settings.values: 0 gives square corners; larger numbers give rounder ones. With posts, the keyguard's top corners are square and its bottom corners are rounded by 2 millimeters, whatever this says.
settings.picture: 2 vs 15, with have a keyguard frame = yes, mount keyguard with = snap-in tabs and generate = keyguard
settings.drafter_notes: With posts, the frame's opening gets square corners all round while the keyguard's bottom corners are rounded, leaving small gaps at the bottom corners. A code comment says this is on purpose, so the keyguard is less likely to catch.

settings.name: mount_keyguard_with
settings.tip: How the keyguard attaches to the frame. Snap-in tabs click into grooves, so keyguards can be swapped quickly. Posts at the top edge let the keyguard flip up out of the way.
settings.when: Choose posts when someone needs to lift the keyguard to use the screen without it; keep snap-in tabs when you want to swap keyguards for different apps.
settings.values: With posts, the posts are as thick as the keyguard. If the status bar, upper message bar or upper command bar is exposed, the keyguard is trimmed to the bottom edge of the lowest of them, with the posts at its new top edge.
settings.picture: snap-in tabs vs posts, with have a keyguard frame = yes, have a case = yes and generate = keyguard
settings.drafter_notes: Page 6870 says the keyguard is trimmed to the bottom of the upper command bar; the code trims it only when a top bar is exposed, and otherwise puts the posts at the keyguard's own top edge. The posts and the trim are added only when have a case is yes, but the frame's post slots are cut either way.

settings.name: snap_in_tab_on_top_edge_of_keyguard
settings.shown_as: snap in tab on top edge of keyguard
settings.tip: Yes adds a small snap-in tab to the middle of the keyguard's top edge, which clicks into a groove in the frame. Used only when mount keyguard with is snap-in tabs.
settings.when: Set it to no when the keyguard doesn't reach the top edge of the frame; otherwise the tab is left floating on its own and causes printing problems.
settings.values: This changes only the keyguard. The frame's groove is cut either way.
settings.picture: yes vs no, with have a keyguard frame = yes and generate = keyguard, close-up of the top edge (the tab sticks out less than 1 millimeter)

settings.name: snap_in_tab_on_bottom_edge_of_keyguard
settings.shown_as: snap in tab on bottom edge of keyguard
settings.tip: Yes adds a small snap-in tab to the middle of the keyguard's bottom edge, which clicks into a groove in the frame. Unlike the other tabs, it is also added when mounting with posts.
settings.when: Set it to no when the keyguard doesn't reach the bottom edge of the frame; otherwise the tab is left floating on its own and causes printing problems.
settings.values: This changes only the keyguard. The frame's groove is cut either way.
settings.picture: yes vs no, with have a keyguard frame = yes and generate = keyguard, close-up of the bottom edge (the tab sticks out less than 1 millimeter)
settings.question: With posts, the designer still adds this tab. Is that so a flip-up keyguard clicks shut at the bottom? The draft says so, but nothing documents it.
settings.drafter_notes: With posts, the code still adds this tab (only its pointed ridge, not the small block behind it), presumably so the bottom of a flip-up keyguard clicks shut. That purpose is inferred; no page says so.

settings.name: snap_in_tabs_on_left_and_right_edges_of_keyguard
settings.shown_as: snap in tabs on left and right edges of keyguard
settings.tip: Yes adds a small snap-in tab to the middle of the keyguard's left and right edges, which click into grooves in the frame. Used only when mount keyguard with is snap-in tabs.
settings.when: Set it to no when the keyguard doesn't reach the left and right edges of the frame; otherwise the tabs are left floating on their own.
settings.values: This changes only the keyguard. The frame's grooves are cut either way.
settings.picture: yes vs no, with have a keyguard frame = yes and generate = keyguard, close-up of a side edge (the tab sticks out less than 1 millimeter)
settings.drafter_notes: Page 6870 only discusses turning off the top tab; turning off the side tabs for the same reason is inferred.

settings.name: post_tightness_of_fit
settings.tip: How snugly the frame's slots hold the keyguard's posts. Larger numbers make the slots smaller and the fit tighter, by 0.1 millimeter per step. Only the frame changes.
settings.when: Change it after a test print if the keyguard takes too much force to flip up (lower it) or won't stay up (raise it).
settings.values: At 10 the slots are 1 millimeter smaller across than the posts; at -10 they are 1 millimeter larger. Only the frame needs reprinting. Negative numbers can make the slots break through the top of a frame that is only a little thicker than the keyguard.
settings.note: the larger the number the tighter the fit, affects only the keyguard frame
settings.picture: -10 vs 10, with have a keyguard frame = yes, mount keyguard with = posts and generate = keyguard frame, close-up of a post slot seen from below

settings.name: post_extension_distance
settings.tip: How far each post sticks out past the keyguard's left and right edges into the frame, in millimeters. The frame's pockets for the posts grow to match.
settings.when: Leave it as it is unless the posts need to reach further into the frame to hold, or the frame beside the keyguard is too narrow for the pockets.
settings.values: From 1 to 5 millimeters. Used only when mount keyguard with is posts.
settings.picture: 1 vs 5, with have a keyguard frame = yes, have a case = yes, mount keyguard with = posts and generate = keyguard, seen from above
settings.question: No page describes this one, so "when you'd change it" is worked out from the designer. Is it right?
settings.drafter_notes: No page describes this setting, so the situations in 'when' are inferred from the code.

settings.name: show_keyguard_with_frame
settings.tip: Yes shows the keyguard inside the frame as a see-through pink copy while generate is set to keyguard frame, so you can check how the two fit. It is never part of the exported file.
settings.when: Turn it on while you adjust keyguard height, keyguard width and the slide settings, so you can see the keyguard and the frame together.
settings.picture: no vs yes, with have a keyguard frame = yes and generate = keyguard frame, seen from an angle
settings.drafter_notes: Page 6870 says to set it back to no before rendering and exporting the frame. The code never puts the copy into the exported file, so that step looks no longer needed.

settings.name: keyguard_vertical_tightness_of_fit
settings.tip: Makes the keyguard that fits in the frame slightly taller (positive) or shorter (negative), in millimeters, for a tighter or looser fit. The frame doesn't change.
settings.when: Change it after a test print if the keyguard is too hard to press into the frame (lower it) or falls out too easily (raise it).
settings.values: From -1 to 1 millimeter, in steps of 0.1. The change is to the keyguard's overall height, half at the top edge and half at the bottom. Used only when have a keyguard frame is yes.
settings.note: adjusts the keyguard height, the larger the number the tighter the fit
settings.picture: none: the largest change is 1 millimeter in overall height, too small to see in a side-by-side picture
settings.drafter_notes: Page 6870 says this slider is in Special Actions and Settings and that 10 adds 1 millimeter; in the code it is in this section, the range is -1 to 1, and 1 adds 1 millimeter. The code also shifts the case opening's top and bottom edge positions used by the openings-and-additions file by a tenth of this value, even without a frame; this looks left over from the old scale.

settings.name: keyguard_horizontal_tightness_of_fit
settings.tip: Makes the keyguard that fits in the frame slightly wider (positive) or narrower (negative), in millimeters, for a tighter or looser fit. The frame doesn't change.
settings.when: Change it after a test print if the keyguard is too hard to press into the frame (lower it) or falls out too easily (raise it).
settings.values: From -1 to 1 millimeter, in steps of 0.1. The change is to the keyguard's overall width, half at the left edge and half at the right. Used only when have a keyguard frame is yes.
settings.note: adjusts the keyguard width, the larger the number the tighter the fit
settings.picture: none: the largest change is 1 millimeter in overall width, too small to see in a side-by-side picture
settings.drafter_notes: Page 6870 says this slider is in Special Actions and Settings and that 10 adds 1 millimeter; in the code it is in this section, the range is -1 to 1, and 1 adds 1 millimeter. The code also shifts the case opening's left and right edge positions used by the openings-and-additions file by a tenth of this value, even without a frame; this looks left over from the old scale.

settings.name: cut_cell_openings_and_bars_through_frame
settings.shown_as: cut cell openings and bars through frame
settings.tip: Yes cuts the grid's cell openings and exposed bar openings through the frame wherever the frame covers part of the screen. No leaves the frame solid there.
settings.when: Leave it on when the keyguard is smaller than the screen, or slid within the frame, so the cells under the frame can still be reached; turn it off for a solid frame.
settings.values: It has no effect unless the frame overlaps the screen and the design has a grid. Screen openings you add yourself are cut through the frame either way.
settings.note: cut the grid cell openings and exposed bars through the frame (wherever the frame overlaps the screen)
settings.picture: yes vs no, with have a keyguard frame = yes, keyguard width = 150 (so the frame covers the outer columns of the default grid) and generate = keyguard frame, seen from above

settings.name: split_line_location
settings.tip: Where the keyguard is cut in two, in millimeters from its middle. 0 lets the designer choose a line between the two middle columns of cells (rows in portrait).
settings.when: Change it when the automatic split doesn't suit the design, for example to move the cut onto a wider strip of plastic between cells or so that each half fits your printer.
settings.values: Positive numbers move the split right in landscape, or up in portrait; negative numbers move it left or down. A keyguard frame, or a keyguard with no grid, is split at its exact middle when this is 0.
settings.picture: 0 vs 40, with show split line = yes and generate = keyguard, seen from above
settings.drafter_notes: For a frame in portrait, the code cuts at the mirror image of where the split line is shown: a positive number moves the shown line up but the actual cut down. This looks like a bug. Also, a split at the exact middle of a keyguard with a grid can't be asked for, since 0 means automatic; 0.1 comes close.

settings.name: show_split_line
settings.tip: Yes shows a thin see-through pink line where the split will fall, and the Console reports how far it is from each side. The line is never part of the exported file.
settings.when: Turn it on while you choose the split line location, to check that each half will fit your printer.
settings.note: set this option to "no" before rendering your design
settings.picture: no vs yes, with generate = keyguard, seen from above
settings.question: Its gray note says to set it to no before rendering, but the designer never puts the line in the exported file now. Drop the note? (The Keyguard Frame page has the same old step for show keyguard with frame.)
settings.drafter_notes: The existing note says to set this to no before rendering. The code treats the line like the pink highlights and never puts it in the exported file, so the warning looks out of date (page 1787 repeats it). It is marked fold because it is obsolete, not because the tip repeats it; Ken to confirm.

settings.name: split_line_type
settings.tip: How the two halves of a split keyguard meet. Flat is a straight cut that you glue. Dovetails is a row of interlocking teeth for a stronger joint.
settings.when: Choose dovetails for a stronger joint when the strip of plastic where the split falls is wide enough: ideally 6 millimeters or more, and no less than 4.
settings.values: With dovetails, the first half gets the teeth and the second half the matching sockets; dovetail width, slide dovetails and tightness of dovetail joint then apply. The teeth are 2 millimeters deep.
settings.picture: flat vs dovetails, with generate = first half of keyguard, seen from above
settings.drafter_notes: The 4 and 6 millimeter guidance comes from page 1787, not the code.

settings.name: dovetail_width
settings.tip: The width of each dovetail tooth along the split line, in millimeters. Wider teeth are spaced further apart, so there are fewer of them.
settings.when: Change it, along with slide dovetails, when a tooth at the top or bottom edge, or beside an opening, leaves a small piece disconnected or hanging by a thread.
settings.values: From 3 to 6 millimeters. Used only when split line type is dovetails.
settings.picture: 3 vs 6, with split line type = dovetails and generate = first half of keyguard, close-up of the joint
settings.drafter_notes: Page 1787 calls it approx dovetail width and places it in Special Actions and Settings; it is now dovetail width in this section.

settings.name: slide_dovetails
settings.tip: Moves the whole row of dovetail teeth along the split line, in millimeters, without moving the split itself.
settings.when: Change it when a tooth at the top or bottom edge, or beside an opening, leaves a small piece disconnected or hanging by a thread.
settings.values: In landscape, positive moves the teeth up; in portrait, positive moves them right. From -3 to 3 millimeters. Used only when split line type is dovetails.
settings.picture: -3 vs 3, with split line type = dovetails and generate = first half of keyguard, close-up of where the split meets the top edge

settings.name: tightness_of_dovetail_joint
settings.tip: How tightly the dovetail joint fits. Larger numbers make the sockets in the second half narrower, for a tighter fit. Only the second half changes.
settings.when: Change it after printing a test joint: lower it if the halves won't push together, raise it if they are loose. A looser joint leaves room for glue.
settings.values: From -0.5 to 0.5 millimeter: each socket gets that much narrower (positive) or wider (negative) in all. The second half is the right half in landscape and the bottom half in portrait, and it is the only half to reprint.
settings.note: the larger the number the tighter the fit, affects only the second half of the keyguard
settings.picture: none: the largest change is half a millimeter in the width of each socket, too small to see in a side-by-side picture

settings.name: add_sloped_keyguard_edge
settings.tip: Yes shapes the keyguard's outer edge to rest on the sloped border of a case or screen protector, reaching out over the slope beyond the case opening. Needs have a case set to yes.
settings.when: Turn it on when the hard border around the case opening slopes down to the screen and leaves no room for slide-in tabs.
settings.values: The keyguard grows by the horizontal and vertical sloped edge widths on each side, or to the full case size with extend lip to edge of case. Set keyguard thickness to at least case to screen depth, or the edge stops short of the top of the slope and clip-on straps are left off.
settings.note: can only be applied to 3D-printed, rounded-rectangular keyguards
settings.picture: no vs yes, with have a case = yes and keyguard thickness = 6, seen from below at an angle
settings.drafter_notes: The code uses the case opening measurements without checking have a case; with have a case = no it would build from a zero-size opening. With have a keyguard frame = yes, the slope is applied to the frame and also to the keyguard inside it, which then grows to the frame's full size; this looks unintended.

settings.name: sloped_edge_starting_height
settings.tip: How high above the screen the slope begins at the edge of the case opening, in millimeters. Use 0 when the border slopes all the way down to the glass.
settings.when: Set it to the height of the short straight step, if any, at the inner edge of the case's border before it starts to slope.
settings.values: The keyguard's underside rises straight up this far at the edge of the case opening, then follows the slope up to case to screen depth.
settings.picture: 0 vs 3, with add sloped keyguard edge = yes and keyguard thickness = 6, seen from below at an angle
settings.drafter_notes: The code does not stop it being set at or above case to screen depth, where there would be no slope left.

settings.name: horizontal_sloped_edge_width
settings.tip: How far the slope reaches out from the left and right edges of the case opening, in millimeters, measured looking straight down. Without a lip, the keyguard grows this much on each side.
settings.when: Set it to the measured width of the sloped border on the left and right sides of the case opening.
settings.values: Measure it flat across, not along the slope. With extend lip to edge of case set to no, the keyguard ends at the outer edge of the slope.
settings.picture: 5 vs 15, with add sloped keyguard edge = yes and keyguard thickness = 6, seen from above
settings.drafter_notes: Page 21145 says every measurement must be the same on all four sides; the code now accepts one width for the left and right sides and another for the top and bottom. The outer corners use the smaller of the two widths.

settings.name: vertical_sloped_edge_width
settings.tip: How far the slope reaches out from the top and bottom edges of the case opening, in millimeters, measured looking straight down. Without a lip, the keyguard grows this much at each edge.
settings.when: Set it to the measured width of the sloped border along the top and bottom of the case opening.
settings.values: Measure it flat across, not along the slope. With extend lip to edge of case set to no, the keyguard ends at the outer edge of the slope.
settings.picture: 5 vs 15, with add sloped keyguard edge = yes and keyguard thickness = 6, seen from above
settings.drafter_notes: Page 21145 says every measurement must be the same on all four sides; the code now accepts one width for the top and bottom and another for the left and right sides. The outer corners use the smaller of the two widths.

settings.name: case_to_slope_depth
settings.tip: With extend lip to edge of case set to yes: how much higher than the top of the slope the rest of the case's surface sits, in millimeters. The lip's underside is raised by this much.
settings.when: Set it when the sloped border ends below the surface of the rest of the case, so the lip that reaches the case's edge rests on that surface.
settings.values: Use 0 when the slope ends level with the case. It has no effect when extend lip to edge of case is no. The keyguard must be thicker than case to screen depth plus this amount, or the lip is cut away entirely.
settings.picture: 0 vs 2, with add sloped keyguard edge = yes, extend lip to edge of case = yes and keyguard thickness = 8, seen from below at an angle
settings.drafter_notes: In the code, the top of the slope is at case to screen depth and the lip sits this much higher, so case to screen depth must be measured to the top of the slope, not to the top of the case. Page 21145 explains this setting only in a picture, so the direction (case higher than the slope) comes from the code alone.

settings.name: slope_gap
settings.tip: Lifts the keyguard's sloped underside off the sloped border by this many millimeters, leaving room for tape. Negative numbers count as 0.
settings.when: Add a gap when you attach the keyguard with micro-suction or double-sided tape thicker than about half a millimeter.
settings.values: The gap is measured straight up, not square to the slope. The part of the keyguard over the screen doesn't change.
settings.picture: 0 vs 1.5, with add sloped keyguard edge = yes and keyguard thickness = 6, close-up of the edge seen from the side

settings.name: extend_lip_to_edge_of_case
settings.shown_as: extend lip to edge of case
settings.tip: Yes extends the keyguard past the slope all the way to the outer edge of the case, using case height, case width and case corner radius from the Tablet Case section.
settings.when: Turn it on when you want the keyguard to cover the whole face of the case, rather than stop where the sloped border meets the rest of the case.
settings.values: No: the keyguard stops at the outer edge of the slope. Yes: a flat lip covers the rest of the case's face, raised by case to slope depth if the case sits higher than the top of the slope.
settings.picture: no vs yes, with add sloped keyguard edge = yes, have a case = yes and keyguard thickness = 6, seen from above

settings.name: text
settings.tip: Words to engrave into the keyguard or raise from its surface. Leave it empty for no text. The other settings in this section set where it goes and how it looks.
settings.when: When you want a label on the keyguard, such as a name or the app page it was made for.
settings.values: Engraved text that falls over a cell opening is lost in the opening; the text also shows as a see-through pink shape in the 3D view, so you can check where it lands. On a laser-cut keyguard the text isn't drawn in the SVG file; the Console lists it, with its size and position, for whoever cuts the keyguard.
settings.picture: "" vs "ABC", with text height = 10, slide horizontally = 50, slide vertically = 50 and number of rows = 0, so no cell opening swallows the letters
settings.drafter_notes: Text is never added to a keyguard frame, only to the keyguard (the code marks it as unsupported, lines 2620-2621).

settings.name: text_height
settings.tip: The size of the letters, in millimeters, roughly the height of a capital letter. The font is Liberation Sans.
settings.when: When the text is too small to read or feel, or too large for the space it has to fit in.
settings.note: measured in millimeters
settings.picture: 5 vs 12, with text = ABC placed as for text
settings.drafter_notes: OpenSCAD treats this number as the approximate height above the baseline; capitals may come out a little shorter. I did not measure a render.

settings.name: font_style
settings.tip: Plain, bold, italic, or bold italic letters. Bold strokes are thicker, which helps small engraved or raised text stay readable.
settings.when: When plain letters look too thin at the size you need, or you want the text to stand out.
settings.picture: normal vs bold, with text = ABC and text height = 12, placed as for text

settings.name: keyguard_location
settings.tip: Which face of the keyguard gets the text, top or bottom. Bottom-surface text is mirrored so it reads correctly when you turn the keyguard over.
settings.when: Leave it at top surface unless you want the text on the side that faces the screen.
settings.values: Bottom-surface text can only be engraved: a positive text depth puts nothing there. A laser-cut keyguard takes text on the top surface only.
settings.picture: top surface vs bottom surface, with text = ABC placed as for text, both seen from below

settings.name: show_back_of_keyguard
settings.tip: Yes turns the 3D view over so you look at the bottom of the keyguard, to check text on the bottom surface. Only the view changes, not the keyguard.
settings.when: When you have put text on the bottom surface and want to see it.
settings.values: While it is yes, the view turns back over after every change you make, and keyguard display angle is ignored.
settings.picture: none: it turns the view, not the keyguard (for a view picture: no vs yes, with text on the bottom surface)
settings.drafter_notes: In the web app the toolbar's bottom-view button shows the same thing without a setting, so this setting may matter mostly in desktop OpenSCAD.

settings.name: keyguard_region
settings.tip: The part of the keyguard the text is placed on: the screen, the case opening, or the whole tablet. Slide horizontally and slide vertically measure across this part.
settings.when: When the text should sit in the border outside the screen: case region if there is a case, tablet region if there isn't.
settings.values: Each choice measures from its own lower-left corner: the screen's, the case opening's, or the tablet's. Case region needs a case; without one, the text lands in the middle of the keyguard whatever the slide settings say.
settings.picture: screen region vs case region, with have a case = yes, text = ABC, text horizontal alignment = left, text vertical alignment = bottom, slide horizontally = 0, slide vertically = 0 and number of rows = 0 (the text moves from the screen's corner to the case opening's corner)
settings.drafter_notes: Raised text (a positive text depth) in the tablet region never reaches the keyguard: the code only engraves there (lines 2315-2336 both test for a negative depth), though the pink preview still shows it. Looks like a bug.

settings.name: text_depth
settings.tip: How deep the letters are cut, in millimeters, written as a negative number: -2 cuts them 2 millimeters into the keyguard. At 0 there is no text.
settings.when: When engraved letters are too shallow to see or feel, or you want raised letters instead.
settings.values: A more negative number cuts deeper. A positive number raises the letters that many millimeters above the top surface. On a laser-cut keyguard the number is ignored, and the person cutting it chooses the depth.
settings.note: positive numbers for embossed text, only on top surface
settings.picture: -2 vs 2, with text = ABC placed as for text (engraved vs raised)
settings.drafter_notes: Nothing stops an engraving deeper than the keyguard; from the code it would cut the letters right through, and the middles of letters like O and A would fall out. Not test-rendered.

settings.name: text_horizontal_alignment
settings.tip: Which part of the text sits at the point set by slide horizontally: its left end, its middle, or its right end.
settings.when: When text near a side edge runs off the keyguard: use left near the left edge and right near the right edge.
settings.values: Left makes the text run to the right of the point, right makes it run to the left, and center splits it evenly. With a vertical text angle it works along the text, so it shifts the text up or down.
settings.picture: left vs right, with text = ABC, slide horizontally = 50, slide vertically = 50 and number of rows = 0

settings.name: text_vertical_alignment
settings.tip: Which part of the text sits at the point set by slide vertically: its bottom, its baseline, its middle, or its top.
settings.when: When text near the top or bottom edge runs off the keyguard.
settings.values: Bottom puts the text above the point and top hangs it below. Baseline is the line the letters sit on, so letters like g and y dip below it. Center splits it evenly.
settings.picture: bottom vs top, with text = ABC, slide horizontally = 50, slide vertically = 50 and number of rows = 0

settings.name: text_angle
settings.tip: Turns the text a quarter turn either way, or upside down. The text turns around the point set by slide horizontally and slide vertically.
settings.when: When the text has to fit a tall, narrow space such as a side border, or be read by someone sitting across from the student.
settings.values: Vertical upward reads from bottom to top, and vertical downward from top to bottom. Horizontal inverted is upside down.
settings.picture: horizontal vs vertical upward, with text = ABC placed as for text

settings.name: slide_horizontally
settings.tip: Where the text sits from left to right, as a percent of the width of the part chosen in keyguard region: 0 is its left edge, 50 the middle, 100 the right edge.
settings.when: Whenever you add text, to move it onto solid plastic rather than over a cell opening.
settings.values: This sets the point that text horizontal alignment works from, so with the default center alignment, 0 leaves half the text past the left edge. On the bottom surface it measures from the left as you look at the bottom.
settings.note: % of screen, case opening, or tablet width
settings.picture: 20 vs 70, with text = ABC, slide vertically = 50 and number of rows = 0

settings.name: slide_vertically
settings.tip: Where the text sits from bottom to top, as a percent of the height of the part chosen in keyguard region: 0 is its bottom edge, 50 the middle, 100 the top edge.
settings.when: Whenever you add text, to move it onto solid plastic such as a rail or the border.
settings.values: This sets the point that text vertical alignment works from, so with the default center alignment, 0 leaves half the text below the bottom edge.
settings.note: % of screen, case opening, or tablet height
settings.picture: 20 vs 70, with text = ABC, slide horizontally = 50 and number of rows = 0

settings.name: Braille_location
settings.tip: Where the Braille goes on a cell insert: above, below, left or right of its round opening, or on both sides. Used when generate is set to cell insert.
settings.when: When you make Braille cell inserts and want the Braille on a particular side of the opening, or two Braille words, one on each side.
settings.values: The two-sided choices put the first Braille element above or to the left and the second below or to the right, and leave out engraved text. With engraved text, a one-sided choice puts the text on the opposite side. Left and right leave less room, often only one or two letters.
settings.picture: above opening vs above and below opening, with generate = cell insert and Braille text = yes,no

settings.name: Braille_text
settings.tip: The words to turn into Braille dots on a cell insert. Only letters and spaces become Braille, and capital letters come out the same as small ones.
settings.when: When you make cell inserts for a student who reads Braille.
settings.values: The first element goes where Braille location says. A second element, after the comma, is used only by the above and below and the left and right choices. Empty makes an insert with no Braille, which comes out lying flat rather than standing on edge.
settings.note: separate Braille elements with a comma and no space
settings.picture: "" vs "yes", with generate = cell insert
settings.drafter_notes: Digits and punctuation aren't in the designer's Braille table; I believe they are dropped, but did not confirm how OpenSCAD handles a character it can't find. There are no capital signs, number signs or contractions (page 6474 agrees). That an insert with Braille is made standing on edge is presumably its print orientation; the code doesn't say why (line 2107).

settings.name: Braille_size_multiplier
settings.tip: Scales the Braille dots and their spacing in tenths: 12 makes them 20 percent larger, 8 makes them 20 percent smaller. Engraved text on the insert scales with them.
settings.when: When the student needs larger Braille, or the Braille is too wide to fit on the insert.
settings.values: At 10 a Braille letter is about 6.5 millimeters tall and letters are 6.1 millimeters apart.
settings.note: 10 = standard size Braille
settings.picture: 8 vs 14, with generate = cell insert and Braille text = yes
settings.drafter_notes: Nothing checks that the Braille fits on the insert; a large size or a long word can run past its edges.

settings.name: add_circular_opening
settings.tip: Yes cuts a round hole through the cell insert, so the student can still reach the button beneath it. No makes the insert solid.
settings.when: Set it to no when the insert should cover its cell completely.
settings.values: With no, the Braille and engraved text stay where they would be with the hole, so a blank space is left where the hole would have been.
settings.picture: yes vs no, with generate = cell insert
settings.question: Is the round hole there so the student can press the button through the insert? The draft says so, but nothing documents it.
settings.drafter_notes: That the hole is for pressing the button through is my reading; neither the code nor page 6474 says what it is for.

settings.name: diameter_of_opening
settings.tip: How wide the round hole in the cell insert is, in millimeters, at the bottom where it meets the screen. The hole widens toward the top.
settings.when: When the hole is too small for the student's finger, or so large it crowds the Braille.
settings.values: A larger hole pushes the Braille and engraved text out toward the insert's edges. With a 4 millimeter thick insert, the hole comes out about 2.7 millimeters wider at the top than at the bottom.
settings.picture: 6 vs 14, with generate = cell insert
settings.drafter_notes: Page 6474 says the top is 2 mm wider than the bottom. The code cuts a cone that grows 4 mm across over the insert's thickness plus 2 mm, so with a 4 mm insert the hole is about 0.7 mm wider than this number at the bottom and about 3.3 mm wider at the top. The setting is close to, not exactly, the bottom diameter.

settings.name: Braille_to_opening_distance
settings.tip: The space between the Braille and the round opening on a cell insert, in millimeters. It is ignored when the insert also has engraved text.
settings.when: When the Braille sits too close to the opening to read comfortably, or too far from it to fit on the insert.
settings.values: A larger number moves the Braille away from the opening. The Braille and the opening stay centered on the insert as a pair.
settings.picture: 2 vs 8, with generate = cell insert, Braille text = yes and Braille location = above opening
settings.drafter_notes: The code adds 1 mm to this number and measures to just beyond the hole's top edge (lines 4965, 4973), so the gap you see is about 1.3 mm more than the setting.

settings.name: engraved_text
settings.tip: Words in ordinary letters to engrave on the cell insert, on the side opposite the Braille, for teachers and communication partners who don't read Braille.
settings.when: When the people working with the student need to see what each Braille insert says.
settings.values: The letters are bold, cut 1 millimeter deep, and 8 millimeters in size at the standard Braille size, scaling with Braille size multiplier. They appear only with the one-sided Braille locations; above and below and left and right leave them out.
settings.picture: "" vs "YES", with generate = cell insert, Braille text = yes and Braille location = above opening
settings.drafter_notes: Nothing checks that the text fits; long text can run past the insert's edges.

settings.name: insert_tightness_of_fit
settings.tip: Makes the cell insert a little larger, for a tighter grip in its cell, or smaller, for an easier fit. At 1 it is half a millimeter wider and taller.
settings.when: When a printed insert falls out of its cell, or is too tight to push in.
settings.values: Positive numbers make the insert bigger and tighter; negative numbers make it smaller and looser. At 0 it is exactly the size of the cell opening.
settings.note: the larger the number the tighter the fit
settings.picture: none: the whole range changes the insert by only a millimeter, too little to see in a picture
settings.drafter_notes: At 0 there is no clearance at all, so how well 0 fits depends on the printer.

settings.name: insert_recess
settings.tip: Makes the cell insert thinner than the screen area of the keyguard by this many millimeters, so its face sits below the keyguard's surface.
settings.when: When you want the insert's face to sit below the top of the keyguard rather than level with it.
settings.values: 0 makes the insert as thick as screen area thickness. Larger numbers make it thinner.
settings.picture: 0 vs 2, with generate = cell insert, seen from the side
settings.drafter_notes: The Braille dots don't move with the recess: they stay where the full-thickness face would be (line 9185). At standard size, a recess of more than about 1.5 mm leaves the dots floating off the insert's face, and smaller recesses make them stand up higher. Worth a test render before advising Braille with a recess.

settings.name: unit_of_measure_for_screen
settings.tip: Whether the numbers for screen openings are pixels, read off a screenshot, or millimeters, measured on the screen. Case openings are always in millimeters.
settings.when: Set it to the unit you measured your screen openings in, before you enter them.
settings.values: px: pixels, as read off a screenshot of the whole screen. mm: millimeters, measured from the app's edge, which is the screen's edge unless keyguard inset mode is on. Changing it while Custom Openings is open converts the openings there so they stay put; otherwise the numbers already entered are read in the new unit, and the openings move and change size.
settings.note: px = pixels, mm = millimeters
settings.picture: px vs mm, with one 40 by 40 rectangle at x 60, y 60 in my screen openings: small and near the corner as pixels, much larger and farther in as millimeters
settings.drafter_notes: The User Manual, section 4.3 step 1, presents this as the unit for the bar heights in App Layout. In the code it affects only screen openings and additions (and the matching values offered to the openings-and-additions file); the bar heights, cell sizes and padding have their own units, and which App Layout section is used depends on whether any App Layout in px value is above 0 (line 1214). Changelog agrees: labels were changed to reinforce that unit of measure and starting corner only apply to screen openings.
settings.source: keyguard.scad 414, 583, 1160-1161, 1187-1188, 1214, 5135-5153, 5360-5451; app.html 8404-8460 (ogConvertScreenUnits: converts only while the panel is open); pages 21866, 23179; manual 4.3

settings.name: starting_corner_for_screen_measurements
settings.tip: Which corner of the screen the positions of screen openings are measured from. Upper-left matches how picture editors count pixels on a screenshot. Case openings always use lower-left.
settings.when: Leave it at upper-left for measurements taken from a screenshot; choose lower-left if you measured up from the bottom of the screen, for example with a ruler.
settings.values: upper-left: positions count down from the top. lower-left: positions count up from the bottom. Positions across count from the left either way. Changing it moves openings already entered, because their numbers are then read from the other corner.
settings.note: which corner is (0,0)?
settings.picture: upper-left vs lower-left, with unit of measure for screen = mm and one 40 by 40 rectangle at x 60, y 30 in my screen openings: near the top, then near the bottom
settings.drafter_notes: 'Case openings always use lower-left' means the lower-left corner of the case opening, per page 21866; the tip shortens it.
settings.source: keyguard.scad 416, 1270-1275, 1333-1334, 5151-5153, 5374-5470, 5764-5871, 6640; app.html 8370-8400 (corner change relabels, does not convert); pages 21866, 10191

settings.name: include_screenshot
settings.tip: Yes shows a screenshot of the AAC app under the keyguard in the 3D view, so you can check that each opening sits over its button.
settings.when: While you design, to check the openings against the app before you print.
settings.values: In the web app the picture is a PNG or JPEG in your project folder, and with more than one, a picker in the 3D view chooses. In desktop OpenSCAD it is the SVG file named in screenshot filename.
settings.note: set this option to "no" before rendering your design
settings.picture: none: it adds a picture to the view, not to the keyguard (for a view picture: no vs yes, with a screenshot in the project folder, seen from the top)
settings.question: Its gray note matters only in desktop OpenSCAD: the web app never puts the screenshot in an export. Keep the note for OpenSCAD users, or drop it?
settings.drafter_notes: The gray note is for desktop OpenSCAD, where the screenshot can end up in the rendered keyguard. The web app always leaves the screenshot out of the keyguard and its exports, so there the note is unnecessary; it could go if the words are only ever read in the web app.

settings.name: screenshot_filename
settings.tip: Desktop OpenSCAD only: the name of the SVG screenshot file to show under the keyguard. The web app hides this setting and uses the picture in your project folder.
settings.when: Only in desktop OpenSCAD, when your screenshot file isn't named screenshot.svg.
settings.note: screenshot SVG file name
settings.picture: none: a file name
settings.drafter_notes: Hidden in the web app at every skill level. Desktop OpenSCAD looks for the file beside the keyguard designer file; I did not check whether a path to another folder works.

settings.name: keyguard_display_angle
settings.tip: Tilts the 3D view to show the keyguard as the student sees it on a tablet propped up at this many degrees. Only the view changes, not the keyguard.
settings.when: When you want to judge how the keyguard, or a keyguard in its frame, looks from where the student sits.
settings.values: 0 leaves the view alone, and 90 looks straight at the keyguard as if the tablet stood upright. While it is above 0, the view returns to this angle after every change. Show back of keyguard overrides it.
settings.picture: none: it turns the view, not the keyguard (for a view picture: 0 vs 45)
settings.drafter_notes: I read the view as someone looking level at the tablet; the code sets the camera to 90 degrees minus this angle (line 1756).

settings.name: unequal_left_side_of_case_opening
settings.shown_as: unequal left side of case opening
settings.tip: When the screen isn't centered side to side in the case opening: the gap, in millimeters, from the left edge of the case opening to the left edge of the screen.
settings.when: When the case holds the tablet off center, or the keyguard sits off center in a soft case, so all the openings miss their buttons toward one side.
settings.values: 0 means the screen is centered. The keyguard keeps its size and its openings shift to match where the screen really is. It does nothing without a case, and it turns off add symmetric openings.
settings.picture: 0 vs 10, with have a case = yes and the default case opening, where the centered left gap is about 19 millimeters (the openings shift toward the left edge)
settings.drafter_notes: A value of 0 or less counts as centered (line 1086), so a screen right against the case opening's left edge can't be described.

settings.name: unequal_bottom_side_of_case_opening
settings.shown_as: unequal bottom side of case opening
settings.tip: When the screen isn't centered top to bottom in the case opening: the gap, in millimeters, from the bottom edge of the case opening to the bottom edge of the screen.
settings.when: When the case holds the tablet higher or lower than center, so all the openings miss their buttons up or down.
settings.values: 0 means the screen is centered. The keyguard keeps its size and its openings shift up or down to match the screen. It does nothing without a case, and it turns off add symmetric openings.
settings.picture: 0 vs 11, with have a case = yes and the default case opening, where the centered bottom gap is about 7 millimeters (the openings shift up)
settings.drafter_notes: A value of 0 or less counts as centered (line 1087). Page 1064 once calls this "unequal bottom side of case", which is the name of a different setting, the one for clips.

settings.name: unequal_left_side_of_case
settings.tip: For clips: when the case's outer rim is wider on one side, the width in millimeters from the outside left edge of the case to the left edge of its opening.
settings.when: When you make horizontal clips for clip-on straps and the case's left and right rims are different widths.
settings.values: At 0 you get one clip that fits both sides. Any other number gives a pair, a left clip and a right clip that reach different distances, when generate is a horizontal clip, mini clip or micro clip. It doesn't change the keyguard.
settings.picture: 0 vs 10, with generate = horizontal clip and the default case (one clip vs a left and right pair)
settings.drafter_notes: The pair ignores the sloped keyguard edge settings, which do change the single clip's reach (lines 1503-1506 vs 1877-1879). The box has no step setting and a whole-number default, so its arrows may move in steps of 1.

settings.name: unequal_bottom_side_of_case
settings.tip: For clips: when the case's outer rim is wider at the top or bottom, the height in millimeters from the outside bottom edge of the case to the bottom edge of its opening.
settings.when: When you make vertical clips for clip-on straps and the case's top and bottom rims are different heights.
settings.values: At 0 you get one clip that fits both edges. Any other number gives a pair, a bottom clip and a top clip that reach different distances, when generate is a vertical clip, mini clip or micro clip. It doesn't change the keyguard.
settings.picture: 0 vs 15, with generate = vertical clip and the default case (one clip vs a bottom and top pair)
settings.drafter_notes: As for unequal left side of case. Also, for the vertical mini and micro clips the line that sets the pair apart gives a four-number position (lines 1951, 1997), which OpenSCAD probably rejects, so the two clips may be drawn on top of each other. Looks like a bug; not test-rendered.

settings.name: move_screenshot_horizontally
settings.tip: Slides the screenshot left (negative) or right (positive) under the keyguard, in millimeters, to copy how the printed keyguard misses its buttons. The keyguard doesn't move.
settings.when: When a printed keyguard's openings all sit off their buttons toward one side even though your measurements look right.
settings.values: It needs include screenshot set to yes. Once the picture is off in the same way as the real keyguard, the Console gives a number for unequal left side of case opening; enter it, then set this back to 0.
settings.note: see instructions in Console pane
settings.picture: none: it moves the screenshot in the view, not the keyguard (for a view picture: 0 vs 10, with include screenshot = yes)
settings.drafter_notes: The Console's advice calls this setting "move screen horizontally" (line 1103). It adds the move to the centered gap and ignores any value already in unequal left side of case opening, so a second round of adjustment would undo the first; page 1064 implies it builds on your current value. Without a case the advice is a meaningless negative number. A comment in app.html says the .scad moves the picture by a tenth of the value; the .scad moves it by the full value (line 8560), the same as the web app.

settings.name: move_screenshot_vertically
settings.tip: Slides the screenshot down (negative) or up (positive) under the keyguard, in millimeters, to copy how the printed keyguard misses its buttons. The keyguard doesn't move.
settings.when: When a printed keyguard's openings all sit above or below their buttons even though your measurements look right.
settings.values: It needs include screenshot set to yes. Once the picture is off in the same way as the real keyguard, the Console gives a number for unequal bottom side of case opening; enter it, then set this back to 0.
settings.note: see instructions in Console pane
settings.picture: none: it moves the screenshot in the view, not the keyguard (for a view picture: 0 vs 10, with include screenshot = yes)
settings.drafter_notes: Same as move screenshot horizontally: the advice says "move screen vertically" (line 1110), ignores any value already in unequal bottom side of case opening, and is meaningless without a case.

settings.name: keyguard_edge_chamfer
settings.tip: Bevels the top outside edge of the keyguard by this many millimeters so it is less sharp to handle. It also bevels openings outside the screen, such as the camera opening.
settings.when: When the outside edge feels sharp, or set it to 0 for a square edge.
settings.values: 0 leaves the edge square, and larger numbers make a wider 45-degree bevel. Laser-cut keyguards are never beveled.
settings.note: not for use with laser-cut keyguards
settings.picture: 0 vs 3, seen at an angle, close up on an outside corner
settings.drafter_notes: The outside-edge bevel is built in 0.2 mm steps, so 1.1 comes out the same as 1.0, and unlike the opening bevels it isn't limited to the keyguard's thickness (lines 1353-1355, 7383-7387).

settings.name: cell_edge_chamfer
settings.tip: Bevels the top edge of every cell opening, and of other openings over the screen, by this many millimeters so the edges are less sharp.
settings.when: Leave it as it is unless the cell edges feel sharp (raise it) or the bevel eats too far into narrow rails (lower it).
settings.values: 0 leaves square edges. The bevel is 45 degrees, or follows the cell's own slope where that is shallower, and it also bevels the edge of a recessed screen area. Laser-cut keyguards are never beveled.
settings.note: not for use with laser-cut keyguards
settings.picture: 0 vs 2, seen at an angle, close up on the cells

settings.name: hide_screen_region
settings.tip: Yes cuts away the whole screen area, leaving only the keyguard's outer border, as a quick test print of the tablet, case and screen measurements.
settings.when: Before printing a full keyguard for a new tablet or case, to check that the outline fits and the screen, home button and camera are where the design puts them.
settings.values: While it is yes, the mounting cuts on a keyguard without a case, the snap-in tabs and trim to rectangle are left off. A keyguard frame loses its screen area too.
settings.picture: no vs yes

settings.name: first_two_layers_only
settings.tip: Yes keeps only the bottom 0.4 millimeters of the keyguard, two layers at 0.2 millimeters each, for a quick, thin test print of the fit.
settings.when: Before a long print or a costly laser cut, to check the openings against the app on the real tablet, and the fit in the case.
settings.values: Openings that go right through still show, but ridges and other raised features don't. It works on a keyguard frame too.
settings.note: assuming 0.2 mm layers for a total of 0.4 mm
settings.picture: no vs yes, seen at an angle
settings.drafter_notes: The cut is always 0.4 mm whatever layer height your printer uses.

settings.name: trim_to_rectangle_lower_left
settings.tip: With trim to rectangle upper right, keeps only the part of the keyguard inside a rectangle. This is the rectangle's lower-left corner, in millimeters from the keyguard's lower-left corner.
settings.when: When you want to test-print only one part of a keyguard, such as a few cells you keep adjusting.
settings.values: Type the x and y, separated by a comma. Both trim settings must be filled in for either to work; empty both to get the whole keyguard back. It is ignored while hide screen region is yes.
settings.note: specify the lower left coordinate (example: 10,50)
settings.picture: both empty vs 50,40 here with 150,120 in trim to rectangle upper right
settings.drafter_notes: Page 3868 says to type the numbers in square brackets and to reset with [0,0]. Brackets still work, but [0,0] in both boxes now trims away the whole keyguard; emptying the boxes is the reset. Trimming isn't applied to a keyguard frame. The keyguard's lower-left corner is the case opening's corner with a case, and the tablet's corner without one.

settings.name: trim_to_rectangle_upper_right
settings.tip: With trim to rectangle lower left, keeps only the part of the keyguard inside a rectangle. This is the rectangle's upper-right corner, in millimeters from the keyguard's lower-left corner.
settings.when: When you want to test-print only one part of a keyguard, such as a few cells you keep adjusting.
settings.values: Type the x and y, separated by a comma; each must be larger than the lower-left corner's. Empty both trim settings to get the whole keyguard back.
settings.note: specify the upper right coordinate (example: 80,125)
settings.picture: both empty vs 150,120 here with 50,40 in trim to rectangle lower left
settings.drafter_notes: As for trim to rectangle lower left.

settings.name: use_Laser_Cutting_best_practices
settings.tip: Yes holds a laser-cut design to limits for durable acrylic: rounder corners, standard slide-in tabs, and a Console warning when the outer border is under 2 millimeters wide.
settings.when: Leave it at yes unless you, or whoever cuts the keyguard, need sharper corners or your own slide-in tab sizes.
settings.values: Yes makes case opening corners at least 2 millimeters in radius, cell corners at least a tenth of the cell's shorter side, and slide-in tabs 1 millimeter thick and 3.175 millimeters long. No uses your own settings and warns only below 1 millimeter. 3D-printed designs aren't affected.
settings.picture: yes vs no, with type of keyguard = Laser-Cut, case opening corner radius = 0 and cell corner radius = 0 (rounded vs square corners)
settings.drafter_notes: Page 3469 lists more limits under this setting (thickness, slopes, chamfers, mounting methods); in the code those apply to every laser-cut design whatever this says. The page's 3 to 4 mm border advice is stricter than the code's 2 mm warning.

settings.name: other_tablet_general_sizes
settings.tip: For a tablet that isn't in the list: its 21 measurements, in millimeters and separated by commas, taken with the tablet in landscape. Used when type of tablet is other tablet.
settings.when: When the student's tablet isn't in the type of tablet list and you have measured it yourself.
settings.values: In order: tablet width, height and thickness; screen width and height; right, left, bottom and top borders; distance from screen to home button, home button height, width and location; distance from screen to camera, camera height, width and location; then the top-left, top-right, bottom-left and bottom-right corner radii. A location is 0 for none, or 1 to 4 for the top, right, bottom or left edge.
settings.picture: none: without all 21 numbers, and the 3 in other tablet pixel sizes, nothing is drawn, so there is no pair of values to compare
settings.drafter_notes: With the wrong count in either box no keyguard is drawn, and the Console says which box is short (lines 1774-1784). Page 358 says to paste the numbers between brackets; the code takes them with or without.

settings.name: other_tablet_pixel_sizes
settings.tip: For a tablet that isn't in the list: the screen's pixels on its short side, its pixels on its long side, and the size of one pixel in millimeters. Used with other tablet.
settings.when: Together with other tablet general sizes, when you have measured a tablet that isn't in the list.
settings.values: The pixel size matters most. If you can't find it, divide the screen width in millimeters by its width in pixels, and check that against the height.
settings.picture: none: as for other tablet general sizes

settings.name: my_screen_openings
settings.tip: Openings and additions over the screen, written as rows like the screen openings in the openings-and-additions file. Custom Openings fills this in when you save.
settings.when: When you use Custom Openings, or want a design's own openings saved with its preset rather than in the openings-and-additions file, which every design in the folder shares.
settings.values: Positions follow unit of measure for screen and starting corner for screen measurements, as in the file. These rows are added to any in the file, and a name the designer doesn't recognize stops the keyguard from drawing until it is fixed.
settings.note: O&A file alternative
settings.picture: "" vs one rectangle row, [1,"r",30,50,3,100,75,0,"C","T",0,0,[],[]], with unit of measure for screen = mm and number of rows = 0
settings.drafter_notes: Custom Openings edits only plain rectangles, circles and straight ridges here; any other rows are kept as typed (app.html 7797-7812).

settings.name: my_case_openings
settings.tip: Openings and additions outside the screen, in millimeters from the case opening's lower-left corner, in the same rows as the file's case openings. Custom Openings fills this in.
settings.when: When the design has a case and needs an opening outside the screen, such as for a button or sensor on the tablet or case.
settings.values: Ignored without a case. These rows are added to any in the openings-and-additions file, and a name the designer doesn't recognize stops the keyguard from drawing.
settings.note: O&A file alternative
settings.picture: "" vs one row, [1,"r",10,8,2,9,85,0,"C","T",0,0,[],[]], with have a case = yes (a small opening in the left border)
settings.drafter_notes: Custom Openings shows these only on its pixels or millimeters tab (manual 7.2), and edits only plain rectangles and circles.

settings.name: my_case_additions
settings.tip: Shapes added to or cut from the keyguard's outside edge so it matches a case opening that isn't a plain rectangle, in the same rows as the file's case additions.
settings.when: When the case opening has bulges, notches or a curved side, or you need slide-in tabs or strap pedestals where the standard mounting can't put them.
settings.values: Measured in millimeters from the keyguard's lower-left corner, and ignored without a case. These rows are added to any in the openings-and-additions file; Custom Openings doesn't edit them.
settings.note: O&A file alternative
settings.picture: "" vs one row, [1,"c",40,0,0,0,85,0,[]], with have a case = yes (a rounded bulge on the middle of the left edge)
settings.drafter_notes: Example row not test-rendered. In a keyguard frame the code doesn't check for a case before applying some of these shapes (lines 2607-2618), so 'ignored without a case' may not hold for frames.

settings.name: my_tablet_openings
settings.tip: Openings outside the screen on a keyguard without a case, in millimeters from the tablet's lower-left corner, in the same rows as the file's tablet openings.
settings.when: When a keyguard that covers the whole tablet needs an opening the tablet settings don't make, such as over a sensor or button on the bezel.
settings.values: These rows are added to any in the openings-and-additions file, and Custom Openings doesn't edit them. A name the designer doesn't recognize stops the keyguard from drawing. With a keyguard frame, the frame gets these openings instead.
settings.note: O&A file alternative
settings.picture: "" vs one row, [1,"c",8,0,0,10,30,0,"C","T",0,0,[],[]], with have a case = no (a small round hole in the left border)
settings.drafter_notes: The code doesn't require 'no case'; with a case the openings are still measured from the tablet's corner (lines 2306-2308).

faults.title: Light-sensor openings in the wrong place on three current iPad families.
faults.what: Since version 78 (April 28, 2026), a mistyped comment in the light-sensor table hides one entry and moves every later one up a place. The iPad Pro 13-inch (M4, M5) gets the iPad Air 11-inch openings, the iPad Air 11-inch (M2 to M4) gets the iPad Air 13-inch ones, and the iPad Air 13-inch (M2 to M4) gets the Tobii-Dynavox I-16's. Expose ambient light sensors is yes by default, so these keyguards have small holes where there is no sensor and cover the real ones, which can upset the screen's automatic brightness. The Tobii-Dynavox I-16 gets no sensor openings at all, because its name is also spelled differently in the lookup.

faults.title: No mounting holes in portrait.
faults.what: In portrait, Suction Cups, Velcro and Screw-on Straps put no holes or recesses on the keyguard at all, with no warning. In landscape all three appear.

faults.title: An empty laser-cutting file with Velcro or Suction Cups.
faults.what: On a laser-cut keyguard with either of those mounting methods, the file for the laser cutter comes out empty, while the 3D view shows a keyguard with the mounting quietly left off. Raised Tabs and Clip-on Straps at least say they aren't supported for laser cutting.

faults.title: No slide-in tabs with a keyguard frame.
faults.what: With a frame and Slide-in Tabs, the tabs are placed on the inner edge of the frame, inside its border, so neither the frame nor the keyguard has any. Raised Tabs on a frame come out right.

faults.title: A portrait frame is split on the wrong side.
faults.what: When a keyguard frame is split in portrait, it is cut at the mirror image of the split line shown: 30 above the middle cuts 30 below. Landscape frames and portrait keyguards are cut where the line shows.

faults.title: A sloped edge with a frame, or without a case.
faults.what: With a frame, the keyguard meant to fit inside it comes out full case-size and larger than the frame, so it can't fit. With have a case set to no, the keyguard comes out as a 20 millimeter square, with no warning.

faults.title: Raised text in the tablet region is never added.
faults.what: Raised (embossed) text placed in the tablet region doesn't reach the keyguard or its export, though the 3D view shows the letters. Engraved text there, and raised text in the screen region, both work.

faults.title: One clip of a vertical mini or micro pair is upside down.
faults.what: When the pair is made, one of the two vertical mini clips (or micro clips) is turned upside down and sits below the print bed. The horizontal pairs are fine.

faults.title: Braille dots come loose from a recessed insert.
faults.what: The Braille dots don't move back with the insert's face when insert recess is used: at 1 millimeter they stand out on a thin neck, and past 1.5 millimeters they float free of the insert. Also, on a 25 millimeter cell, the top row of dots hangs half off the insert's top edge.

faults.title: Add symmetric openings does nothing without a case.
faults.what: Without a case it changes nothing on an iPad 9th generation, because the tablet's built-in borders differ by about a hundredth of a millimeter. And on a laser-cut keyguard with light sensors turned off, the mirrored sensor holes are cut anyway, on one side only.

faults.title: Trim to rectangle with 0,0 trims away everything.
faults.what: Both corners set to 0,0 (with or without brackets) leaves no keyguard at all; empty boxes leave it whole. The Keyguard for a PC Keyboard page gives [0,0] as the way to reset it.

faults.title: App Layout in px goes wrong if top of lower command bar is left at 0.
faults.what: The designer then reads all five numbers as counted from the bottom of the screenshot: the status bar comes out about 150 millimeters tall and the grid is squashed into a thin strip along the bottom, with no warning. Entering the screenshot's full height there, as the screenshots page says, gives the right layout.

faults.title: The Console's advice for moving the screenshot.
faults.what: It names settings that don't exist ("move screen horizontally" for move screenshot horizontally), and its suggested value ignores what is already in unequal left (or bottom) side of case opening, so a second round of adjustment undoes the first.

pages.issue: Says the extra plastic is measured in from the edge of the screen; the designer measures it in from the keyguard's own edge. Waits on your answer to the question under top edge compensation for tight cases.
Still names the old settings "height compensation for tight cases" and "width compensation for tight cases"; today there is one per edge.

pages.page: Changing the Slope of a Message/Command Bar Edge
pages.issue: Says a command bar's edge can be sloped too; the designer slopes only a message bar's edge. Waits on your answer to the question under bar edge slope.
Gives the smaller magnet as 20 x 18 x 1.5; the designer's choice is 20 x 8 x 1.5. It also mentions a red shape showing the magnet, which only desktop OpenSCAD draws.

Puts the two tightness-of-fit sliders in Special Actions and Settings, where 10 added 1 millimeter; they're now in Keyguard Frame Info, run from -1 to 1, and 1 adds 1 millimeter. Says posts always trim the keyguard at the bottom of the upper command bar; the designer trims only when a top bar is exposed. Says to set show keyguard with frame back to no before exporting, which is no longer needed.

pages.page: Splitting your keyguard into two pieces for easier printing
pages.issue: Says to set show split line to no before rendering, which is no longer needed, and calls dovetail width "approx dovetail width" in Special Actions and Settings; it's now in Split Keyguard Info.
Says the slope must measure the same on all four sides; the designer now takes one width for the left and right sides and another for the top and bottom.
Once says "unequal bottom side of case" where it means "unequal bottom side of case opening"; the first is a different setting, for clips.

pages.page: Designing a Keyguard to be Laser-Cut
pages.issue: Lists limits (thickness, slopes, chamfers, mounting methods) under use Laser Cutting best practices; they apply to every laser-cut design, whatever that setting says.
Says the round hole is 2 millimeters wider at the top; the designer makes it nearer 3. Minor.
Says to reset trim to rectangle with [0,0], which now trims away the whole keyguard; emptying the two boxes is the reset.

manual.where: Section 4.3, Describe the app's layout, steps 1 and 2
manual.issue: Step 1 says unit of measure for screen sets the unit for the bar heights. It doesn't: it applies only to screen openings. The designer uses App Layout in px when any number there is above 0, and App Layout in mm otherwise. Step 2 says to enter "the height of each bar", which is right for App Layout in mm; App Layout in px takes positions instead, each counted in pixels from the top of the screenshot.
